issues.author: ClassicLarry
issues.body:
Sequence shuffling reduces the 128-step train-loss sawtooth seen with flat-cache training on `hero_tok/v16384_shuf` at batch 1024. In a single-seed S7 d512 comparison, it improves Paloma macro loss by 0.0135 and reduces train-loss autocorrelation at lag 128 from 0.226 to 0.026. A second seed and a batch-256 rung are still needed to confirm the gain size.

The default block shuffle (`BlockShuffleConfig(io_block_size=256, window_blocks=512)`, [datasets.py:574](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/data/text/datasets.py#L574)) gives a 128-step train-loss sawtooth on [s7l-d1280L16](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/s7l-d1280L16), for example +0.11 at step 5504 = 43×128. A window contains 131,072 sequences. Long documents (56.5% of tokens are in documents >4096 tokens, 16.3% in >256k, up to 1.6M) occupy consecutive sequences inside one 256-sequence block. Every slice of a document therefore lands in the same window, and the model sees the same file for 128 steps.

The old cache, `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/datakit/hero_tok/v16384_shuf/train`, contains 124,408,413,939 tokens. Hero store `store_4d2e363d` was decoded to text and sampled by `harrier_mix_2026_08_18.json` (`hero_text`), documents were capped (`hero_text_capped`), tokenized with `hero-bpe-v16384` (`v16384_617680a7`), then shuffled at the document level by `experiments/grug/fast_track/shuffle_cache.py`.

The sequence-shuffled cache, `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/datakit/hero_tok/v16384_seqshuf/train`, packs the old cache into 4096-token sequences exactly as `TokenSeqDataset` reads it, then permutes them with `numpy.random.default_rng(20261020).permutation(30373147)`, one sequence per row ([seq_shuffle_cache.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/marin_belay_v1_fp8quality/experiments/grug/fast_track/seq_shuffle_cache.py), e53d6b0620). Sequence contents are unchanged; only their order changes. Validation found the same sequence and token counts, with 514 sampled sequences byte-identical.

S7 d512, batch 1024, 1346 steps, seed 0, and the default block shuffle were held fixed; only `--train-cache` differs (a5a8647840). [saw5-ctl](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/saw5-ctl) uses the old cache; [saw5-seq](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/saw5-seq) uses the sequence-shuffled cache:

- Paloma macro loss: 2.9322 → 2.9187 (−0.0135)
- Paloma micro loss: 2.6586 → 2.6460 (−0.0126)
- Uncheatable macro loss: 2.3959 → 2.3817 (−0.0142)
- Eval loss: 2.6232 → 2.6103 (−0.0128)
- Paloma macro BPB: 1.2139 → 1.2077 (−0.0062)
- Uncheatable macro BPB: 0.9136 → 0.9075 (−0.0061)
- Eval BPB: 1.0429 → 1.0378 (−0.0051)
- Train-loss autocorrelation at lag 128: 0.226 → 0.026

d512 seed noise is ~0.007 in macro loss. BPB uses the current token-weighted levanter computation, which has a known batching dependence; losses are the primary metric.

Done when ladder and large-batch fast_track runs default to `v16384_seqshuf`, and a second seed and batch-256 rung confirm the gain size.

---

**Relevant code**

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
The simulated-S3 concurrent-writer test intermittently fails while publishing a table schema. In [CI on #10348](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/39533315377/job/119004477743), `test_concurrent_writers_publish_every_row_through_conflicts` reports `ConditionalRequestConflict`, then fails at `assert existing is not None` in [`write_schema`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e4f5b7d0089a4c16ad9cd202a68f15ef4d9b8e79/lib/finestore/src/finestore/commit.py#L128-L146). This fails the Finestore CI lane.

Reproduce:

1. Use main commit `e4f5b7d0089a4c16ad9cd202a68f15ef4d9b8e79`, Python 3.12, and an environment with FineStore's test dependencies installed.
2. From the repository root, run:

   ```bash
   PYTHONPATH="$PWD/lib/finestore/src:$PWD/lib/rigging/src:$PWD/lib/marin/src" \
   uv run --no-sync python -c "import sys, pytest; sys.setswitchinterval(1e-6); raise SystemExit(pytest.main(['-n', '0', '-q', 'lib/finestore/tests/test_simulated_s3.py::test_concurrent_writers_publish_every_row_through_conflicts']))"
   ```

3. Repeat in a fresh process if it passes; the failure depends on thread scheduling.

On the exact, unmodified main source and test, 20 ordinary subprocess attempts passed. With only the Python thread-switch interval reduced to `1e-6`, the second attempt reproduced the same schema conflict and assertion as CI. Source files were verified against the pinned Git blobs. This local reproduction used existing dependencies on macOS; it was not a clean Linux CI rerun or a live-S3 test.

Expected: concurrent writers registering the same schema complete successfully, and the test publishes all 18 rows.

[`SimulatedS3.conditional_write`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e4f5b7d0089a4c16ad9cd202a68f15ef4d9b8e79/lib/finestore/src/finestore/testing/simulated_s3.py#L299-L326) can reject a contending writer while the first writer is still in flight. `write_schema` catches the conflict and immediately rereads the object, assuming it already exists. That read can return `None` before the first writer publishes.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

`DataStore.table()` registers a schema through `write_schema()`. A simulated S3 conditional write can fail while another writer is still in flight, so the immediate reread can return `None` and trigger the assertion. No open PR overlaps this schema conflict.

**Relevant code**
- [`store.py#L237-L249`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e4f5b7d0089a4c16ad9cd202a68f15ef4d9b8e79/lib/finestore/src/finestore/store.py#L237-L249) — table registration
- [`commit.py#L129-L148`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e4f5b7d0089a4c16ad9cd202a68f15ef4d9b8e79/lib/finestore/src/finestore/commit.py#L129-L148) — schema publication
- [`simulated_s3.py#L299-L326`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e4f5b7d0089a4c16ad9cd202a68f15ef4d9b8e79/lib/finestore/src/finestore/testing/simulated_s3.py#L299-L326) — in-flight conflict

# Proposed Fix

`DataStore.table()` calls `write_schema()`, whose conditional write may lose before the winner publishes; the following read then returns `None`. Retry the read/create/validate attempt with bounded backoff after an unresolved conflict, and add a simulated-S3 test that holds the winning write in flight until the losing writer observes the missing schema.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body: 🤖 PR #10413 retries unresolved schema-write conflicts with bounded backoff and adds a deterministic simulated-S3 regression. The new test reproduced the assertion before the fix; all 252 FineStore tests pass after it. Changed-files lint and targeted pyrefly pass; repository-wide pyrefly reports 121 local errors, including missing dependencies.

issues.author: mcwitt
issues.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

MXFP8 on Blackwell is viable for Grug MoE expert GEMMs, but only when the block-scaled quantization producer is fused into the expert-MLP path. Dense matmuls should stay on the delayed per-tensor FP8 path: native dense MXFP8 lowered and produced reasonable numerics, but standalone block quantization erased the GEMM win. The best supported direction is the hybrid recipe now encoded behind `GrugFp8Config(recipe="mxfp8")`: delayed per-tensor FP8 for dense attention/shared MLP matmuls, fused MXFP8 grouped kernels for ragged experts, and `recompute_all` as the production remat mode. The latest EP1 apples-to-apples D6144 run is an important caveat: with FP8 wire communication disabled, MXFP8 was 0.749x BF16 end-to-end on that topology, so the production recommendation still depends on profiling, communication settings, and the #7271 quality/perf gate rather than the early grouped-GEMM microbench alone.

### Helpful links
- Latest EP1 apples-to-apples result: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7282#issuecomment-5037422197
- Uniform MXFP8 feasibility decision: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7282#issuecomment-5028942402
- Research branch: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/research/mcwitt/7282-mxfp8-blackwell
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

Implement and tune a Blackwell-native FP8 path for grug MoE training on B200/GB200, using the hardware's MXFP8 (block-scaled, 32-element blocks with E8M0 scales) tensor-core support instead of the Hopper delayed per-tensor-scaling recipe:

- **Dense GEMMs** (attention q/k/v/o, shared-expert MLP): `jax.nn.scaled_dot_general` / cuDNN-cuBLASLt block-scaled matmuls, replacing `Fp8DotGeneralOp`'s per-tensor path where profitable.
- **Grouped expert GEMMs** (`w13`/`w2` ragged dots): an SM100 block-scaled grouped kernel -- CUTLASS via `cutlass_call` or a Mosaic-GPU tcgen05 port of the Hopper kernels.
- MXFP8 scaling is computed per-block on the fly (stateless -- no amax history), which should simplify the train-step state handling that per-tensor delayed scaling required.

Base: PR #7079 (FP8 end-to-end wiring: #6880 `Fp8RaggedDotOp` expert GMMs, #6660 `Fp8DotGeneralOp` dense GEMMs, FP8 wire collectives, `GrugModelConfig.fp8` + train-step state). The FP8 wire (per-token scaling) is hardware-agnostic and expected to carry over unchanged.

Part of the #6998 "Sanity Check FP8 training on Blackwell" work stream. This issue tracks the implementation and kernel/perf tuning; the compute-optimal training quality check (MXFP8 vs BF16, wall-time matched) is #7271 and consumes this work.

## Hypothesis or Goal

MXFP8 on B200 matches or beats the Hopper per-tensor FP8 speedups at the canonical grug shape (d2560/F1280/E256/K4): grouped GEMMs >=1.3x vs bf16 at the layer level, dense GEMMs >=1.2x isolated, with a simpler stateless recipe and numerics adequate for #7271's regression gate.

## Status

E2E goal met for the early d2560/L26/B64 GB200x4 configuration (MXFP8-005, 2026-07-17): mxfp8 beat bf16 and per-tensor fp8 under `recompute_all`, with loss parity near 4e-4/step. Later production-shape checks added caveats: uniform dense MXFP8 is not ready in the current distributed stack, and the latest EP1 D6144 same-config pair showed MXFP8 slower than BF16 when FP8 wire communication was disabled. Treat the hybrid path as promising but still gated on topology-specific profiling and #7271.

## Links

* Logbook: `.agents/logbooks/mxfp8-blackwell.md` (on the research branch)
* Branch: [`research/mcwitt/7282-mxfp8-blackwell`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/research/mcwitt/7282-mxfp8-blackwell)
* W&B Report:
* Important updates:
  * Latest EP1 apples-to-apples result: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7282#issuecomment-5037422197
  * Uniform MXFP8 feasibility decision: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7282#issuecomment-5028942402

## Decision Log

- 2026-07-16 (mcwitt): stay on MXFP8 for its numerics upside; push perf to per-tensor class rather than falling back to a per-tensor grouped kernel. (Logbook: "Direction decision", MXFP8-002c.)
- 2026-07-16: dense GEMMs stay on per-tensor `Fp8DotGeneralOp`; dense mxfp8 shelved unless #7271 shows per-tensor numerics insufficient. (MXFP8-001b.)
- 2026-07-17 (mcwitt): benchmark only production-viable configs (>120B total / >15B active). The #7012 slim-vjp/`all_but_moe` port is dropped -- those modes OOM 3-12x at the d5120/L48/b1024 64-GPU reference config (#7012 branch logbook, B200MFU-032), leaving `recompute_all` (already our benchmark mode) as the production mode. New top item: MXFP8-006 production-shape ladder. (Logbook: "production-viability filter" entry.)
- 2026-07-21 (mcwitt): same-source, same-config EP1 D6144 pair found MXFP8 at 0.749x BF16 with FP8 wire disabled; do not use the earlier EP-confounded comparisons as isolated MXFP8 effects.

## Conclusion

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Update: background research brief (MXFP8-000b) — foraging done, vehicles chosen

- Change: four-track prior-work pass (pinned-JAX source probe, NVIDIA MXFP8 recipe, SM100 grouped-GEMM survey, internal corpus). Full brief with evidence map and source ledger in the logbook (`.agents/logbooks/mxfp8-blackwell.md` @ 61aa41d0f).
- Key findings:
  - Our jax 0.10.1 pin already has the complete dense MXFP8 path: `jax.nn.scaled_dot_general` with a real custom_vjp (dgrad and wgrad both run as block-scaled matmuls), custom_partitioning, and ceil-rounded E8M0 scales; gpu-extra lockfile ships cuDNN 9.19 (floor 9.7.1). Footguns: `configs=None` silently falls back to bf16; residuals are stored full-precision.
  - Correct recipe (NVIDIA arXiv 2506.08027, matches TE and the jax defaults): E4M3 for everything including gradients (E5M2 grads degrade MXFP8 — opposite of our Hopper per-tensor finding), round-UP E8M0 scales, dual rowwise+columnwise quantized copies from the high-precision original.
  - Grouped vehicle: pinned nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.5.2 ships an MXFP8 MoE scaled-grouped-GEMM kernel (`CuTeDSL .../moe/torch_scaled_grouped_mm.py`) — offs-ragged 2Dx3D fwd + 2Dx2D wgrad, shape-for-shape our ragged_dot decomposition; NVIDIA measured 1.29-1.41x vs the cuBLAS grouped path on B200. Plan: vendor it behind the existing `cutlass_call` FFI adapter from the fp8-ragged-cute branch (sm_100a). Mosaic tcgen05 (fully plumbed in our jaxlib, incl. block-scaled MMA) is the bake-off second entrant.
  - Expectation bound from #7012's step anatomy: MoE GEMMs are ~24% of the single-node step, so the e2e MXFP8 ceiling is ~1.1x there; layer-level targets (grouped >=1.3x, dense >=1.2x) remain the gate. Grouped bf16 baseline on B200 is QuACK/Triton (XLA ragged_dot has no SM100 path).
  - FP8 wire stays bf16 during the MXFP8 phase (NVIDIA EP quantizes after dispatch); re-test later.
- Confidence: recipe/API claims high (installed source + paper + TE agree); grouped-kernel perf is NVIDIA's own table, unreplicated here.
- Links:
  - Commit: 61aa41d0f (logbook brief), branch `research/mcwitt/7282-mxfp8-blackwell`
  - Related: #7012 (baselines), #5816 (older B200 FP8 issue), PR #7079 (base)
- Next: MXFP8-001 — B200 env probe + dense microbench (`scaled_dot_general` vs bf16 vs per-tensor `Fp8DotGeneralOp` at grug dense shapes, plus numerics check vs bf16 reference).

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Update: MXFP8-001 (dense microbench, 1x GB200) — surprising first result

- Change: ran the dense GEMM microbench (bf16 vs per-tensor fp8 vs native mxfp8 `jax.nn.scaled_dot_general`) at row-13 dense shapes (T=65536; qkvo 2560x2560, shared-expert 2560<->1280) on cw-us-east-08a GB200, jax 0.10.1 / cuDNN 9.19.
- Result delta:
  - Native mxfp8 WORKS (lowers to `__cudnn$blockScaledDot`; rel-err ~3.7e-2, slightly better than per-tensor fp8) but is SLOWER than bf16: 0.82-1.00x fwd, 0.64-0.81x fwd+bwd. The compiled HLO shows XLA materializing the quantized block tensors with standalone kernels around the cuDNN GEMM — quantize overhead is the prime suspect, especially on bwd (cotangent re-quantized for both grad legs).
  - Per-tensor `Fp8DotGeneralOp` — the dense path PR #7079 already wired — is excellent on sm100: 1.35x fwd / 1.61x fwd+bwd at qkvo (1990 / 2363 TF/s vs bf16's 1471). Better than its H100 showing. For dense GEMMs the merged per-tensor path is the incumbent on Blackwell.
- Confidence: exploratory (single GPU, single run; GB200 not B200, same sm100 compute die).
- Links:
  - Commit: 6d3cf1a02 (harness `experiments/grug/moe/standalone/bench_mxfp8_dense.py`), logbook entry MXFP8-001 @ 91b0a1973
  - Job: /mwittmann/mxfp8-001-dense-r3 on cw-us-east-08a
- Next: MXFP8-001b — isolate GEMM-only throughput via `jax.nn.scaled_matmul` with precomputed quantized operands+scales. If the bare blockScaledDot beats bf16, mxfp8 dense is rescuable with a fused quantizer; if not, dense stays per-tensor fp8 and MXFP8 effort concentrates on the grouped expert GEMMs (CUTLASS DSL kernel).

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Update: MXFP8-001b — GEMM-only isolate; dense decision made

- Change: added a `scaled_matmul` arm with operands quantized outside the timed region (job /mwittmann/mxfp8-001b-dense-r2, 1x GB200), isolating the `__cudnn$blockScaledDot` GEMM from XLA's quantize kernels.
- Result delta:
  - GEMM-only mxfp8 is healthy: 1.33x vs bf16 at qkvo 2560x2560, 1.11-1.14x at the narrow shared-expert shapes.
  - The culprit is quantization: XLA's emitted block-quantize kernel costs 0.26-0.36 ms per operand (~a full GEMM's worth, roughly 1 TB/s effective on ~8 TB/s HBM). On the backward pass the cotangent is quantized twice, hence MXFP8-001's 0.65-0.79x e2e.
  - Even with a free quantizer, mxfp8 GEMM-only merely ties per-tensor fp8 (1.33 vs 1.35 at qkvo; loses at narrow shapes). Per-tensor delayed scaling is structurally cheaper: no amax reduction in the hot path, and its scalar multiply+cast fuses into neighboring ops.
- Decision: dense GEMMs on Blackwell stay on the per-tensor `Fp8DotGeneralOp` path that PR #7079 already wired (1.35x fwd / 1.5-1.6x fwd+bwd measured here). Native-mxfp8 dense is shelved unless #7271's quality gate later shows per-tensor numerics are insufficient (mxfp8's error is only marginally better: 3.7e-2 vs 4.3e-2 rel-Frobenius). MXFP8 effort now concentrates on the grouped expert GEMMs, where sm100 has no working fp8 path at all.
- Confidence: exploratory (single GPU, single run each), but the quantize-overhead decomposition is internally consistent across all three shapes.
- Links: logbook entries MXFP8-001b + hypothesis queue @ branch `research/mcwitt/7282-mxfp8-blackwell`.
- Next: MXFP8-002 — vendor the CuTeDSL MoE scaled-grouped-GEMM kernel (pinned cutlass-dsl 4.5.2) behind the fp8-ragged-cute `cutlass_call` adapter; correctness vs emulated reference, then bench vs QuACK bf16 at row-13 expert shapes.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Update: MXFP8-002 — MXFP8 grouped GEMM working from JAX on GB200 at 2.2 PF/s

Not yet covered: dgrad/wgrad products and the quantize+swizzle producer — the bench builds scale factors with a slow gather; MXFP8-001b showed naive quantization can eat the entire win, so a fused quantize+swizzle kernel is the critical path to a layer-level fwd+bwd claim.

🤖 Update: MXFP8-002b — all three GEMM products green; the quantizer now decides everything

- Change: extended the grouped-kernel port with dgrad (2Dx3D, transposed-weight view via TensorSpec — no materialized transpose) and wgrad (the kernel's 2Dx2D scenario, natural layouts, TMA-aligned for any group sizes), plus a fused dual-orientation quantize+swizzle producer in pure XLA. Commits 92f7af921, b6fa1f9de; job /mwittmann/mxfp8-002b-g1 (single job, first-attempt green).
- Result delta (M=262144, E=64, GB200, errors all 3e-6..1e-5 vs dequantized ref):
  - fwd 2130/2027 TF/s (w13/w2), dgrad 2041/2112, wgrad 2209/2214 — every product ~1.4-1.5x over the bf16 dense yardstick. wgrad is the fastest product.
  - Honest layer-quad (fwd+dgrad+wgrad for w13+w2 vs 3x bf16 dense = 6.95 ms): GEMMs alone 4.86 ms = 1.43x; adding the XLA quantize producers (7.06 ms for 4 activation + 2 weight tensors) drops it to 0.58x — a net loss. XLA quantization runs at ~1.6-2.2 TB/s and cannot get near the 2.09 ms break-even.
  - Producer budget math: an HBM-ideal standalone dual-write quantizer (~1.4 ms) yields only ~1.11x; a fusion-grade producer (quantize folded into ops that already touch the tensors, ~0.7 ms marginal) yields ~1.25x. Same conclusion as the Hopper thread, where the dual-write cast-transpose kernels were what made FP8 pay.
- Confidence: exploratory but internally consistent (independent quantize measurements in MXFP8-001b and 002b agree).
- Links: logbook entry MXFP8-002b (incl. gotchas: 2Dx2D SF atom-block permutation, zero-token-expert epilogue semantics), branch `research/mcwitt/7282-mxfp8-blackwell`.
- Next: MXFP8-002c — prototype the fused dual-write MXFP8 quantizer (CuTe/Mosaic, Hopper cast-transpose analog) targeting <=0.7 ms marginal for the activation tensors. This is the 0.58x-vs-1.25x decision point; op wiring (MXFP8-004) follows the verdict.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Update: MXFP8-002c — CuTe dual-write quantizer lands the layer at break-even; decision point

- Change: implemented and validated a CuTe DSL dual-orientation MXFP8 quantizer (one bf16 read -> rowwise+columnwise e4m3 copies + e8m0 scales; integer-only round-up exhaustively validated; no transpose stage needed since wgrad consumes natural-layout columns). Jobs /mwittmann/mxfp8-002c-g1..g11; commits 68bbe7d5a..189c3faf0.
- Result delta:
  - Bit-exact vs the corrected reference on all outputs including adversarial blocks. Along the way it exposed a real bug in the XLA reference: GPU `jnp.exp2` is inexact on 217/256 e8m0 exponent bytes — the reference had been quantizing with wrong scales at extreme exponents (fixed in adapter.py; never decode e8m0 via exp2).
  - Producer cost for the 4 activation tensors: 2.074 ms vs 5.19 ms XLA (2.5x), effective ~4.8 TB/s. Layer-quad: 0.58x -> **1.00x** (weights amortized; 0.80x if XLA weight producers run every microbatch).
  - The <=0.7 ms fusion-grade target (=> ~1.25x) is out of reach for any standalone kernel: this design is instruction-issue bound with a ~1.4 ms ceiling. Epilogue-fusion probe says SwiGLU+dual-quantize fusion into the grouped GEMM's epilogue is feasible but a targeted rewrite (~1-2 weeks; single elementwise hook exists, no multi-output mechanism, needs w13 column interleave + SIMT side-stores).
- Where this leaves the thread — three options, ranked by expected value:
  1. **Per-tensor-scaled fp8 grouped kernel on sm100** (new hypothesis MXFP8-H7): the recurring lesson (dense MXFP8-001b, grouped 002c) is that block scaling pays a producer tax per-tensor scaling doesn't — per-tensor quantize fuses into XLA for free, so the ~1.4x GEMM-level win should survive at layer level. tcgen05 also supports mixed e5m2xe4m3 natively (no wgmma same-dtype restriction), enabling the numerically-correct backward the Hopper path had to approximate. Moderate port (same vendoring pattern as 002, which went smoothly).
  2. Epilogue fusion for mxfp8 (~1.25x, 1-2 weeks of kernel work).
  3. Wire MXFP8-004 with the break-even producer now (removes producers as dominant cost; useful if mxfp8's numerics are the priority for #7271 regardless of speed).
- Ops notes: GB200 nodes are heterogeneous for libNVVM (`nvvm.cvt.packfloat` fails on most nodes, passes on some — inline PTX bypasses); CPU-only sm_100a compile does not exercise the pod's libNVVM stage.
- Confidence: exploratory; producer/GEMM numbers each replicated within-job across shapes and routing distributions.
- Links: logbook entries MXFP8-002c + hypothesis queue, branch `research/mcwitt/7282-mxfp8-blackwell`.
- Next: awaiting direction on the 3-way choice above; H7 is the recommended default.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Update: direction — pushing MXFP8 to per-tensor-class perf; kernel survey finds the fusion upstream (MIT)

- Change: per owner direction, staying on MXFP8 (numerics rationale) and pushing performance; ran a third-party-kernel survey (tokamax source deep-dive + TE/QuACK/CUTLASS/triton/DeepGEMM/fal.ai web track). Full brief in the logbook (MXFP8-000c).
- Key findings:
  - **cudnn-frontend >=1.21 ships MIT-licensed CuTeDSL fused MoE grouped kernels** — `grouped_gemm_swiglu_quant` (grouped GEMM -> SwiGLU -> dual-orientation MXFP8 quantize with swizzled SFs + per-expert amax), plus dSwiGLU+quant, plain quant-epilogue, and wgrad variants. Same file lineage as the kernel we vendored in MXFP8-002. This is exactly the epilogue fusion MXFP8-002c estimated at 1-2 weeks, already written and maintained by NVIDIA (their blog: 1.3x fwd / 2.1x bwd kernel-level on GB200).
  - Standalone-quantizer path formally closed: even a perfect 6.2 TB/s dual-orientation quantizer leaves producers at ~1.6 ms vs the 0.7 ms fusion-grade target. Every credible implementation gets there via epilogue fusion.
  - tokamax (user question): no MXFP8 on any arch, in any version — sm90 quantized ragged_dot is weight-only dequant-to-bf16 (no fp8 tensor cores on Hopper at all), sm100 kernels are W4A8 inference with float subchannel-128 scales, and there is no sm100 wgrad kernel. MXFP8-on-Hopper generally: no prior art anywhere, and the wgmma arithmetic caps it at ~bf16 throughput — recorded as a dead end.
  - Ceiling check: measured cuBLAS mxfp8 dense tops out at ~2.5-2.7 PF/s (not the 4.5 spec number); our 2.0-2.2 PF/s grouped is ~80% of the honest ceiling. The remaining headroom is in fused epilogues + scheduler, not the mainloop.
- Next (in flight):
  - MXFP8-004a: vendor the cudnn-frontend fused kernels behind our proven cutlass_call adapter (prerequisite: bump nvidia-cutlass-dsl past <4.6 and re-run the 002c bit-exactness suite). Gate: layer-quad >=1.2x vs bf16.
  - MXFP8-004b (time-boxed): bench TE 2.15+ te.jax `grouped_dense` MXFP8 at our shapes — the NVIDIA-tuned narrow-N reference datapoint.
- Links: logbook MXFP8-000c + hypothesis queue (new H8; H5 resolved; Hopper dead-end), branch `research/mcwitt/7282-mxfp8-blackwell`.

🤖 Update: MXFP8-004a/b — fused kernels land the layer at 1.39x vs bf16; gate met

- Change: two parallel results. (a) MXFP8-004a: vendored NVIDIA's MIT-licensed cudnn-frontend fused MoE grouped kernels (SwiGLU+dual-MXFP8-quant fwd, dSwiGLU+quant bwd, quantizing-epilogue GEMM, wgrad; upstream 3041f3e88) into `experiments/grug/moe/standalone/mxfp8_fused/`, driven from JAX via the same cutlass_call adapter pattern — no cutlass-dsl pin bump needed (a 6-site compat shim runs them on stock 4.5.2). (b) MXFP8-004b: TransformerEngine 2.16 grouped_dense MXFP8 benchmarked on the same pod as the NVIDIA-tuned reference.
- Result delta (1x GB200, M=262144, E=64, real gated shapes D2560/F1280):
  - Correctness: swiglu_quant and dswiglu_quant outputs (data + both scale-factor orientations) are BIT-EXACT vs our validated reference; the other legs are at 6e-6..3.6e-5 rel-Frobenius. The fused column-SF layout is byte-identical to what our wgrad kernel consumes — zero glue.
  - Fused layer pipeline (6 GEMM legs + the two remaining x/g2 producers): 8.777 ms vs 12.220 ms for the full bf16 layer (GEMMs + XLA SwiGLU/dSwiGLU) = **1.39x**; 1.13x against a strict 6-GEMM-only yardstick; 1.35x gemm-only. The >=1.2x gate is met on the honest full-layer accounting: the h and dc quantize producers are gone (fused into epilogues), which is what turned MXFP8-002c's 0.58x into a real win. Note the baseline is now the real gated w13 width (2F=2560); earlier half-width numbers aren't comparable.
  - TE reference: cuBLAS grouped MXFP8 GEMM-only 2085/1950 TF/s at our shapes — parity to ~4-12% behind our CuTeDSL kernels; TE's own e2e mxfp8 fwd+bwd is 1.28-1.32x its bf16 and visibly quantize-bound, independently confirming the fusion thesis. (TE V2 MXFP8 grouped also requires every group size %128 — real routing violates this; our kernels don't care.)
  - Remaining headroom, ranked: the dswiglu leg (1244 TF/s; C-read + dual-store epilogue) and folding the x/g2 dual-quant upstream into attention/dgrad epilogues (1.43 ms).
- Confidence: exploratory (single GPU; tiler ablations replicated across nodes; in-sequence timings reported — same-kernel-after-idle measures ~25% faster, a new benchmarking gotcha).
- Links: logbook MXFP8-004a/004b entries (incl. gotchas: arm64-vs-x86 cutlass-dsl wheels differ at the same version; cutlass_call compile failures are process-fatal — probe in subprocess; TE-on-aarch64 install recipe), jobs /mwittmann/mxfp8-004a-g1..g11 and mxfp8-004b-g1..g6, commits aa998a01f..cf979bb4c + 97cf4ac0b.
- Next: MXFP8-004c — wire `MxFp8RaggedDotOp` on the fused kernels into the grug MoE path (256-padded routing), then MXFP8-005 full-step MFU vs the #7012 bf16 baselines.

- Result delta (same-node comparison):

A CPU fake-device probe reproduced a huge arena but turned out to be dominated by reference-attention S^2 buffers (probe artifact — GPU uses FA4), so GPU probes are the decisive ones.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Update: production-shape OOM root-caused — MoE dispatch/combine buffers across the 48 *unrolled* layers; scan-over-blocks port in validation

- Change: diagnosed the 851 GiB step-0 OOM from the first production-shape ladder attempt with compile-only AOT probes on 2-node gangs (XLA memory analysis + buffer-assignment census; the probes never execute, so they measure the arena without holding 32 GPUs).
- Findings, in falsification order:
  - `eqx.error_if` callbacks: falsified (`EQX_ON_ERROR=nan` rerun — arena identical; those checks don't even trace in this config).
  - FA4 per-layer metadata on device 0 (the poison documented in the mcwitt/moe-standalone-ep bench): the fix ports cleanly and is kept, but the arena was unchanged — not the dominant term here.
  - Instruction-keyed census (cache-off dump): the 792 GiB temp arena at d5120/L48/B128 ring-EP8 is the **ring-MoE dispatch/combine buffers of all 48 layers held concurrently live** — full-global-batch combine scatters (`bf16[524288,5120]`, 2/layer) and top4-expanded dispatch buffers (`bf16[262144,5120]`, 5/layer), across the unrolled per-layer subgraphs. Attention and MuonH are not drivers.
  - Scaling: arena is ~linear in global batch (B64 → 340 GiB), so no batch retreat fits the 138 GiB pool; it persists under pure DP (EP1 → 581 GiB).
  - fp8 memory: **mxfp8's arena is 37% smaller than bf16's** (500.82 vs 792.47 GiB, same config) — fp8 is the memory-friendlier arm, not a regression risk.
- Fix in flight: ported the scan-over-stacked-blocks model path (`use_array_stacked_blocks`, from the moe-standalone-ep bench: Bool[num_layers] mask schedule + precomputed FA4 bounds selected by `jnp.where`, traced per-layer rope disable, 4D expert stacks routed through distributed Newton-Schulz). A `lax.scan` bounds the live set to one layer's buffers and should also collapse the 13–40 min lowering times (one traced body instead of 48).
- Confidence: high on the attribution (census names the ops); scan-mode memory number pending the current probe.
- Links:
  - Commits: e8e105d4e (scan port), 0ef1d613c (FA4 bounds), 0a3eda269 (probe tooling); logbook `.agents/logbooks/mxfp8-blackwell.md` entries 2026-07-17 19:40–22:35.
  - Jobs: /mwittmann/mxfp8-006-probe2n{g,i,j,k,s,t,u} on cw-us-east-08a (2-node, 8 GPUs each).
- Next: scan-mode probe memory analysis → if the arena fits, relaunch the 4-arm production-shape ladder (32 GPUs) in scan mode, plus a d2560 loss-parity smoke unrolled-vs-scan.

- Results so far:
  - Baseline replication (their branch, exact env recovered from the controller's job records — EP1+sonic_cute, Muon distribution knobs, NCCL socket-ifname, cuda_async allocator): **609,330 tok/s / 19.63% GB200-MFU** at 128 GPUs vs the published 591,330 / 19.0% — clean reproduction on the same cluster.

issues.title: Experiment: MXFP8 block-scaled GEMMs for grug MoE on Blackwell

issues.author: mcwitt
issues.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

The full hybrid MXFP8 quality gate is complete. BF16 and MXFP8 each trained a d2560/L26/E128/top-4 Grug MoE for 31,474 optimizer steps / 66.006B tokens with the same data order, seed, schedule, optimizer, and 32xGB200 topology. Both arms finished with 8/8 task exits, zero failures or preemptions, final W&B evaluation rows, and audited non-temporary `step-31474` checkpoints.

MXFP8 increased mean non-compile throughput from 788,954 to 845,920 tok/s (+7.220%) and reduced measured runtime to the terminal evaluation by 5,460.6 seconds (91.0 minutes, 6.092%). It also produced slightly higher final losses than BF16: +0.001301 aggregate eval (+0.0562%), +0.002885 Paloma (+0.1105%), and +0.004287 uncheatable (+0.2088%). Aggregate eval favored BF16 at all 32 paired evaluations, and MXFP8 did not reach BF16's final held-out targets within the fixed schedule.

The tested hybrid recipe is therefore a speed-quality tradeoff, not quality-neutral. #7282 subsequently attempted uniform MXFP8 for grouped and dense GEMMs, but the available distributed path aborts before execution at EP2 and EP4. Its training-quality result remains unmeasured.

### Helpful links

- [Final W&B comparison, tables, trajectory chart, and CSV artifact](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/MXFP8Q-007-full-comparison)
- [Detailed experiment logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c189a6a31/.agents/logbooks/mxfp8-quality-7271.md)
- [BF16 full-run W&B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/MXFP8Q-007-full-bf16-s31474)
- [MXFP8 full-run W&B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/MXFP8Q-007-full-mxfp8-s31474)
- [Uniform MXFP8 feasibility result in #7282](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7282#issuecomment-5028942402)
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

Work stream from #6998 ("Sanity Check FP8 training on Blackwell"). Get MXFP8 working for both GMM (MoE expert/ragged matmuls) and dense GEMM on B200, then train a small ~A2B MoE model to compute-optimal and compare against a BF16 baseline on a wall-time-matched basis.

Builds on the prior FP8 work on Hopper (per-token-scaled fp8 ragged dot, #6880) and the B200 MFU work in #7012; Blackwell adds native MXFP8 (block-scaled) tensor-core support, which has not yet been validated in our training stack.

## Hypothesis or Goal

MXFP8 GMM+GEMM training on Blackwell is quality-neutral: a small ~A2B model trained to compute-optimal shows no regression against BF16 when matched on wall time.

## Status

The hybrid quality gate is complete. Both 31,474-step arms succeeded and their terminal W&B histories and S3 checkpoint metadata were verified. MXFP8 delivered a 7.220% throughput gain with a small persistent fixed-token quality cost. It did not reach BF16's final aggregate eval, Paloma, or uncheatable target within the schedule. Uniform grouped+dense MXFP8 quality remains unmeasured because the current distributed implementation aborts before execution; see #7282.

## Links

* Logbook: [mxfp8-quality-7271.md at `c189a6a31`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c189a6a31/.agents/logbooks/mxfp8-quality-7271.md)
* W&B comparison: [MXFP8Q-007 final BF16 vs MXFP8](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/MXFP8Q-007-full-comparison)
* W&B group: [MXFP8 quality group](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/groups/mxfp8-quality-7271)
* Source runs: [BF16](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/MXFP8Q-007-full-bf16-s31474), [MXFP8](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/MXFP8Q-007-full-mxfp8-s31474)
* Implementation: [quality launcher snapshot](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/485e23f7f4d89d1d2f218c777766497d6a8d7ae4), [stabilized smoke implementation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/f8be94f87), [final logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/c189a6a31)

## Decision Log

* Keep stochastic rounding and Hadamard rotation as reserve numerics levers if loss degradation can be attributed to quantization.
* Treat the first smoke's data-loader failure as a shortened-run configuration bug, not a quality result.
* Fix evaluation casting so tagged eval reuses the training cast for ordinary weights while preserving FP8 state.
* Treat the initial hybrid MXFP8 NaN as a w2 weight-gradient issue; stabilize by consuming the fused w2 gradient and recomputing only invalid w2 gradients from BF16 saved operands.
* Launch the full matched 31,474-step pair only after finite 20-step smoke training, forced final evaluation, and checkpointing succeeded.
* Do not classify the tested hybrid recipe as quality-neutral. Its 7.220% throughput gain comes with a small persistent fixed-token quality cost.
* Resume uniform MXFP8 grouped+dense quality work when the distributed backend can execute it; the current EP2 and EP4 paths abort before training (#7282).

## Conclusion

The quality-neutral hypothesis is not supported for the tested hybrid recipe. MXFP8 increased throughput by 7.220% and saved 91.0 minutes, but final aggregate eval / Paloma / uncheatable losses were 0.0562% / 0.1105% / 0.2088% higher than BF16. Aggregate eval favored BF16 at all 32 paired evaluations. MXFP8 finished before BF16 reached step 30,000 and was better than BF16 at that earlier equal-wall-time boundary, but it never matched BF16's terminal held-out targets. Strict time-to-BF16-final-loss is censored rather than improved.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Note for the quality-gate design: two standard numerics levers to keep in reserve if the fp8 arms show loss degradation attributable to quantization. Neither is implemented in our stack today; both are cheap to add and should be tried *before* concluding a recipe is numerically insufficient (or switching the dense recipe wholesale).

1. **Stochastic rounding on cotangents.** Round-to-nearest on quantized gradients introduces a small per-step bias that accumulates over long trainings (loss drift, dead-weight subspaces); stochastic rounding makes the quantization unbiased in expectation, at the cost of an RNG threaded into the gradient quantizers. Standard practice for gradient quantization — qwix exposes per-leg stochastic-rounding hooks (dlhs/drhs noise fns), and NVIDIA's NVFP4 training recipe has SR on by default. Only relevant to the backward; pointless for forward activations.

2. **Hadamard rotation before quantization.** Shared-scale formats (per-tensor fp8, and to a lesser degree 32-block MXFP8) waste resolution when one outlier channel forces a large scale — and LLM activations grow outlier channels as training progresses, especially at the attention projections. Rotating by a Hadamard matrix (orthogonal ±1, O(n log n), exactly invertible through the matmul by folding Hᵀ into the weights) smears outliers across all channels so a shared scale fits well. This is the QuaRot/SpinQuant/Quartet idea; NVIDIA's NVFP4 recipe includes a random Hadamard transform, and qwix ships it as a fused kernel + jax impl. Most valuable as a fix for the *per-tensor dense* legs (attn q/k/v/o, shared expert) — likely cheaper than switching dense to mxfp8, which measured ~2x slower fwd+bwd at our shapes (see #7282, MXFP8-001b).

Suggested gate protocol addition: if an fp8 arm fails the loss bar, attribute first (which legs — dense vs grouped, fwd vs bwd — via selective bf16 fallback), then apply the matching lever (SR for bwd-attributed drift, Hadamard for dense-activation outlier clipping) before rejecting the recipe.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 The full matched-token BF16 vs. hybrid MXFP8 quality gate is complete.

Both arms trained for 31,474 optimizer steps / 66,005,762,048 tokens with the same seed, data order, schedule, optimizer, and 32xGB200 topology. Both eight-task gangs and coordinators succeeded with 8/8 task exits at code `d11d6ac54` (treatment implementation `f8be94f87`, based on the latest #7282 implementation at launch, `c3cb334f8`). W&B finished at zero-based `global_step=31473`, and both arms logged a final region-local `step-31474` checkpoint after all ranks passed storage commit/barrier/error checks. A separate in-cluster audit directly read both checkpoint metadata objects and verified `step=31474` with `is_temporary=false`.

| Terminal metric | BF16 | MXFP8 | MXFP8 − BF16 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Train loss | 1.554700 | 1.557329 | +0.002629 |
| Trailing-100 train loss | 1.581135 | 1.584242 | +0.003107 |
| Trailing-1,000 train loss | 1.594350 | 1.597402 | +0.003052 |
| Aggregate eval loss | 2.314181 | 2.315482 | +0.001301 (+0.0562%) |
| Paloma macro loss | 2.611326 | 2.614211 | +0.002885 (+0.1105%) |
| Uncheatable macro loss | 2.052934 | 2.057221 | +0.004287 (+0.2088%) |
| Mean non-compile tokens/s | 788,954 | 845,920 | +7.220% |
| Post-first-sample runtime to final eval | 89,640.2s | 84,179.6s | −5,460.6s (−91.0 min, −6.092%) |

The quality difference is small but persistent. MXFP8 aggregate eval is higher at all 32 paired evaluations (mean delta +0.002098, range +0.000314 to +0.003768). Paloma and uncheatable are higher at 29/32 evaluations, and all three held-out metrics favor BF16 for the final 26 consecutive gates from step 7,000 through the terminal evaluation.

The speedup does improve quality at earlier equal-wall-time boundaries: MXFP8 finished before BF16 reached step 30,000, and its final aggregate eval / Paloma / uncheatable losses were better than BF16-at-30k by 0.011187 / 0.012284 / 0.009287. However, within this fixed schedule MXFP8 never reaches BF16's exact final aggregate eval, Paloma, or uncheatable target. Strict time-to-BF16-final-loss is therefore censored, not improved.

Conclusion: this recipe gives a stable 1.0722x throughput gain and saves about 91 minutes, but it is not exactly quality-neutral at fixed tokens. The observed cost is +0.056% aggregate eval, +0.110% Paloma, and +0.209% uncheatable at the endpoint.

W&B:

- [Final comparison, tables, trajectory chart, and CSV artifact](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/MXFP8Q-007-full-comparison)
- [BF16 source run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/MXFP8Q-007-full-bf16-s31474)
- [MXFP8 source run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/MXFP8Q-007-full-mxfp8-s31474)
- [Detailed experiment logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c189a6a31/.agents/logbooks/mxfp8-quality-7271.md)

W&B history integrity was checked by reconciling two independent pagination scans: every expected logged train step from 2 through 31,473 was recovered for both arms with no conflicting values, and all 32 paired evaluation rows are present.

This conclusion applies to the tested hybrid recipe (MXFP8 grouped GEMMs plus per-tensor FP8 dense GEMMs). [#7282's uniform grouped+dense attempt](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7282#issuecomment-5028942402) aborts before execution at EP2 and EP4, so its training-quality result remains unmeasured.

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
Current results (October 20): the ten-update smoke completed with a verified checkpoint and Hugging Face export. The longer Smartie Step14 continuation has 61/100 verified optimizer updates. A paired 910-task development evaluation improved across all five families at update 25: equal-family mean verifier score 30.96% → 39.98% under a 4,096-token reply cap. The in-training structural score reached 61.32% at update 50. Datakit SFT and released Dr.Doom comparison runs have loaded their models; baseline evaluation and optimizer updates remain unverified. Those arms use an 8,192-token reply cap, so their scores require budget-matched comparisons. [Current results, protocol and limitations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10314#issuecomment-6298575217).

Build an immutable 100,000-task candidate curriculum for fast-turnaround Snowball RL. Version `2026.10.19.2` contains 88,366 production-admitted TaskSpecs and 11,634 reviewed historical native closure imports. The [private browser](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/e2bd5c9d-0f93-4ce9-b7af-3c78ca55e5d1/v/2/) contains the complete selected pool; sign in with a work Google account.

The approved recipe targets equal shares across five families: 20,000 each. Calendar capacity is 9,115, so its shortfall is distributed over the other four families. Final counts are calendar 9,115; competitive coding 22,722; Reasoning Gym 22,721; STEM 22,721; structural 22,721. This supersedes the initial proposal to reuse [Ben's intended one-sixth/four plus one-third structural weights](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/fed5a9383b92acacbe264c7e601e93d8437218d3/experiments/post_training/smartie/mixture-v2.json).

Sources:

- Calendar: Nemotron calendar and two Task Trove calendar datasets.
- Coding: Nemotron competitive coding, Eurus2, and verified Glaive sandboxes.
- Reasoning Gym: Nemotron puzzles and standalone Reasoning Gym.
- STEM: Nemotron STEM MCQA and OpenScience.
- Structural: all 11,087 selected admitted structured-output tasks plus 11,634 of Ben's synthetic structural-compliance tasks.

The 12 admitted sources have 244,938 eligible contracts after known holdout exclusions. Ben's pinned structural training release adds 57,364 native rows; full-contract deduplication removes 52, leaving 57,312 eligible. Combined candidate population: 302,250. Native additions are sampled as evenly as possible across eight structural families, then their control strata; no row is repeated to fill a quota. Distinct private grading contracts remain distinct and all selected source aliases are retained.

Inputs are pinned in the export:

- Production catalog `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/catalog/production`, snapshot `8c5d247ef6c2416fb3d14b2f159f74c4`; admitted `final/part-*.parquet` identities resolve through the verified CoreWeave migration receipt.
- [Exact historical native data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-Data/tree/cb728a7636caad3fc6fa6b6ba85a49194d9d69a3), with file hashes, native validation IDs and tokenizer-aware prompt identities.
- Four evaluation sources and the known 910-task native validation panel. Native holdout checks use effective token prompts and full contracts, not their shared generic instruction text.

Done when:

- [x] Freeze source revisions, admission/import status, holdouts, recipe, and replay code.
- [x] Exclude known exact holdout overlap; deduplicate complete contracts and retain source aliases.
- [x] Select deterministically without replacement, recording quotas, probability denominators and provisional difficulty labels.
- [x] Publish 100,000 selected contracts, rejection accounting, Parquet, original payloads, readiness, and hashes.
- [x] Implement the historical native closure adapter and validate exact prompts and grading through the current CPU engine/trainer.
- [ ] Publish/pin the updated runtime libraries and trainer, resolve canonical external grader dependencies, and validate actual inference before declaring the complete pool training-ready.

Immutable export: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/curricula/snowball-v0/2026.10.19.2`. Its verified-copy completion manifest covers 20 files, 3,812,705,369 bytes. All published payload hashes match the frozen artifact manifest. Predecessor `2026.10.19.1` remains available unchanged.

Independent validation confirms 100,000 unique task IDs and full contracts, exact family quotas, source/stratum probabilities, retained aliases, and zero known exact holdout overlap. Retained canonical TaskSpec JSON strings are byte-identical to the same task records in the verified predecessor; native payload strings match the pinned historical release. Parquet round trips preserve both formats byte-for-byte. Twenty focused tests, scoped repository lint, and Pyrefly pass. Implementation is tracked in the linked ingester/runtime and trainer PRs.

The immutable pool retains original historical payloads. In its `train.parquet`, `contract_kind` selects either `task_json` or `lowered_task_spec`; the unused payload is null. A separate native adapter now emits 11,634 current `TaskRolloutSpec` records in the trainer’s `task_rollout_spec` column. All selected native tasks passed reference/invalid completions through the current CPU engine (23,268 attempts); all 88,366 canonical identities remain unchanged. The native export passed the actual trainer dataset, and scripted workers covered all eight native families. This is local source/CPU evidence. Published runtime-library releases and trainer lock updates remain release gates. For the smoke, the three adapter packages use exact Git revisions and a separately published full 100,000-task deployment pool. It remaps only the package-lock URI in 51,915 script tasks to a derived historical environment; the expired original dirty-build environment cannot be reconstructed exactly. The remaining 48,085 task payloads, including all native tasks, remain unchanged. The live Linux CPU gate validated the complete pool and returned grades for ten sandbox probes. An earlier GPU attempt failed during model initialization. The subsequent smoke completed ten optimizer updates using the full 100,000-task inventory, sampling 32 shuffled prompts per update with four answers per prompt. Training and export in Hugging Face format succeeded. Final verification checked the step-10 checkpoint commit marker, completed export request, successful terminal manifests, and exported model file inventory against its manifest. This run exercised inference, grading, optimization, checkpoint writing and model export. Checkpoint resume remains untested. A separate continuation with a fresh optimizer has completed 61 of 100 updates; the paired five-family development evaluation improved at update 25, and the in-training structural score improved through update 50. See the current results update linked above for coverage and token-budget limits. Difficulty remains a source/family prior; exact holdout exclusions do not establish semantic decontamination.

The approved derived native component is published at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/curricula/snowball-v0/native-runtime/2026.10.19.1`: nine files, 8,473,539 bytes. Independent full readback matches every frozen SHA-256 and size. Its Parquet contains 11,634 native tasks and does not replace the full 100,000-task pool.

Related: [10k quality/annotation pilot #10315](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10315), [design #10316](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10316).

Implementation: [canonical ingester and runtime support #10319](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10319), following the existing curation catalog and TaskCompendium converter pattern; [trainer companion draft](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/1032). comments.body:
🤖 # Research

The converted release has 4,997,251 training instances, but those counts precede admission, holdout exclusion, and contract deduplication. The four exact NVIDIA components have 13,023 converted instances against roughly 66,667 nonstructural slots in the intended mixture; the structural pool also needs a separate pin. The issue reports no materialized pool, and I could not verify admitted counts without the CoreWeave catalog credentials.

**Relevant code**
- [`catalog_snapshot.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/experiments/post_training/task_curation/catalog_snapshot.py) — catalog snapshot selection
- [`task_curation/README.md`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/experiments/post_training/task_curation/README.md) — admitted output and publication contract
- [TaskSpec input PR #10066](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10066) — trainer input boundary
- [runtime PR #10190](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10190) — current-stack smoke dependency

# Proposed Fix

Follow the selection policy in [#10316](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10316), with these deliverables in order:

1. In the data region, resolve the converted manifest, `production` catalog, each source's admitted `final/part-*.parquet`, holdout IDs, and structural pool to immutable revisions and hashes. Publish an eligibility census by source before choosing expansion sources.
2. Freeze a recipe listing every added source ID and family. Exclude evaluation and known holdout overlap; group identical task and verifier contracts with the existing TaskCompendium identity mechanism. Report eligible counts and rejection reasons, including sources with no admitted rows.
3. Implement and fixture-test seeded selection without replacement: family weights `1/6, 1/6, 1/6, 1/6, 1/3`; square-root weighting across sources in a family; caps and redistribution; and equal coverage of nonempty difficulty strata, retaining `unknown` and provenance. Emit an explicit shortfall if 100,000 unique eligible tasks are unavailable.
4. Publish immutable TaskSpecs, selected identities, source aliases, quotas versus actual counts, rejection accounting, and artifact hashes. Re-run the selector against the same pins to verify identical output.
5. After the TaskSpec input and runtime ports are usable, load the pool on the current stack and smoke roughly 100 distinct tasks covering every selected execution and grader contract. Quarantine failing contracts, reselect, and retain reset/step/grading traces before declaring the pool ready.

The source expansion list, structural-pool pin, and CoreWeave access are prerequisites for the real census and release. The open [#10066](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10066) and [#10190](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10190) PRs cover adjacent input/runtime work; I found no open PR materializing this pool.

issues.author: rjpower
issues.body:
The TaskTrove clean release exposed an incomplete boundary between converted Harbor tasks and post-training execution. Marin publishes packed tasks in Parquet with explicit grader and environment identities. The current MarinSkyRL path expands selected tasks into many individual objects, builds equivalent Daytona snapshots again for each run, and discovers missing egress, resources, or judge configuration after rollout starts.

In the TaskTrove smoke, staging 1,273 tasks as 8,265 files held two H100 nodes idle for 58 minutes before Ray started. A capped 160-task export still required 2,685 objects and 18 minutes. The clean release contains 1,449,686 tasks but only 39 Docker environments, so data selection and environment reuse should be separate operations.

This issue owns the cross-repository contract. Dataset-specific validation remains in marin#9083. MarinSkyRL ingestion and sandbox lifecycle remain in marin-community/MarinSkyRL#540.

Done when:

- A post-training run selects packed tasks using a Parquet URI and metadata predicate, then unpacks only the assigned rows.
- An environment identity includes the Dockerfile, pinned verifier, and sandbox runtime interface. Equivalent environments reuse snapshots across runs and have an explicit cleanup policy.
- Tasks declare required capabilities such as network egress, judge access, and non-default resources. Launch fails before rollout when the selected runtime cannot provide them.
- Publish or launch validation can require an empty workspace to score zero and a shipped golden solution to score one.
- Trial results distinguish solution failure, grader failure, and infrastructure failure.
- Run provenance records the dataset release, selection predicate, verifier identity, and environment identity.
- One deterministic task and one judge task complete through the supported path without per-file corpus staging.

Verifier changes remain versioned with the dataset or environment identity. A wheel may reduce build cost. A training run must preserve the verifier pinned by the published task.

Tracked work:

- [ ] marin#9083: publish-time repository golden checks and judge sampling.
- [x] marin-community/MarinSkyRL#540: Parquet ingestion, environment reuse, capability checks, and judge plumbing.
- [x] marin-community/MarinSkyRL#538: add the `/tokenize` route required by Terminus-2.
- [x] marin#9084: close the snapshot-only ToolScale proposal because the source also leaks its answer.

TaskTrove clean shipped in marin#9061.

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
Add a general prompt audit and repair phase to post-training task curation. It should inspect converted tasks, fix recoverable prompt defects, and retain the evidence needed to review each change. Apply it across sources and future curation rounds, including the Snowball and recursive self-improvement (RSI) task pools.

The original motivating case is this [Eurus2 task](https://gist.github.com/rjpower/f796dac041e7667296af56185d99e593), `eurus2_code-004832f8a66c2fafab97e3d76bfbbc0d6885291f3578e356ec3d95c610e6ad4b`: it imposes named reasoning actions (`[ASSESS]`, `[ADVANCE]`, `[VERIFY]`, `[SIMPLIFY]`, `[SYNTHESIZE]`, `[PIVOT]`, `[OUTPUT]`), numbered steps, and a `Next action:` format. Remove inherited instructions that force an incidental reasoning style while preserving the problem and its grading contract.

The pass should also detect stale role or dataset boilerplate, duplicated or conflicting directives, broken formatting, and missing or mismatched submission/tool instructions. Repair only where the intended task is recoverable from the public task and its declared interfaces. Preserve constraints that define the task, including instruction-following exercises, legitimate procedures, conversation structure, tool protocols, and verifier-required answer formats. Quarantine cases requiring invented context, a changed problem, or a changed grader; record exposed answers as defects and never copy private references, tests, or solutions into prompts.

Done when:

- [ ] Integrate a reusable phase after conversion and before final review, verification, deduplication, and admission. Process every successfully converted task's model-visible messages and instructions, including native imports after lowering to TaskSpec. Retain conversion failures and unsupported cases in the input accounting. Source-level sample acceptance must not imply that unsampled prompts were inspected. Reuse the existing [curation pipeline](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/pipeline/README.md), normalization-change evidence, request caches, and manifests.
- [ ] Define explicit unchanged, repaired, quarantined, and rejected outcomes with defect categories, reasons, and edited spans. Record unavailable or failed review separately from task defects. Bind rule/rubric versions and any model, prompt, and generation settings explicitly; retain model repair proposals and their review decisions.
- [ ] Keep original tasks immutable and publish original-to-repaired ID/hash mappings, source locators, transformation revisions, and before/after examples. Identical pinned inputs/configuration must reuse saved decisions; applying an accepted repair again must produce no further edits.
- [ ] Validate repaired tasks structurally and review that each change preserves task meaning, difficulty-relevant constraints, and the private grading contract. Require unchanged expected verdicts from pinned graders on known-valid and known-invalid submissions for representative original/repaired tasks from every affected source and defect category. Do not claim positive validation from empty/wrong-answer controls alone; keep unresolved repairs out of training-ready output.
- [ ] Recompute identities, full-contract duplicates, and known-holdout overlap for repaired content. Regenerate downstream summaries, embeddings, and review/verification evidence whose inputs changed.
- [ ] Audit a source-stratified panel of repaired and unchanged tasks to check harmful edits and missed defects. Report coverage, outcomes, failures, and counts by source/category against the full input denominator, plus inference cost and timing. Include regression cases for Eurus2, required output/tool formats, intentional instruction constraints, and ambiguous tasks.
- [ ] Pilot the phase with [#10315](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10315), preserving its frozen cohort and denominator. Audit the v0 pool `2026.10.19.2` from [#10314](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10314) and publish a new versioned cleaned pool with its parent manifest hash, quarantine list, and changed-task mappings. For the v0-derived pool, recheck selection quotas and trainer loading; record replacements from pinned eligible candidates under #10314's selection policy, or report the shortfall. Do not refill or replace tasks in #10315's frozen pilot cohort.
- [ ] Document how to enable and rerun the phase for new sources and task-generation rounds, with versioned artifacts and explicit repair policy.

Related: [Snowball curriculum #10316](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10316), [RSI feedback loop #9638](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9638).

Implementation status (2026-10-20): the reusable phase is implemented locally on `codex/prompt-repair-curation` (commits `ef44bcf076` and `737646aae4`; not pushed). SAMPLE/FULL runs opt in with `--prompt-repair-model` and `--prompt-repair-model-revision`; per-task edits retain provenance and require preservation review, original/candidate grader witnesses, and an unchanged re-audit. Local lint and scoped type checks pass; 406 affected tests and the 87-test focused repair/control/cache/source suite passed; the advisory fixes passed a further 85-test repair/source-quality/source-pipeline suite. Both advisory findings are addressed. One full-library `foo`/`FOO` filesystem failure was reproduced against untouched HEAD on macOS. The [initial CPU diagnostic](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fdlwh%2Fprompt-repair-calibration-10350-20261020T1917Z) failed before inference: attempt `/0:0`, UID `50a86d0145a97f37`, exit 1, could not discover a relay registered in another cluster; no report was written.

Calibration (2026-10-20): the [final ten-case panel](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fdlwh%2Fprompt-repair-calibration-10350-v2-20261020) completed inference and saved all decisions, then exited 1 because one decision was invalid. Outcomes: four unchanged, three repaired, three quarantined; nine reviewed, one invalid, zero unavailable. Three clean SVAMP tasks stayed byte-identical. All three synthetic scaffold removals exactly matched the labelled expected TaskSpec hashes; each passed preservation review, original/candidate numeric positive witnesses, empty-submission rejection controls, and an unchanged re-audit. The preservation reviewer could see the synthetic injection tags. These results do not establish source-wide repair quality or nonempty wrong-answer grader parity.

Of three IFEval tasks, one stayed unchanged with its intentional letter-count constraint, one was quarantined for a missing final question, and one proposed removing stale refusal boilerplate while retaining the lowercase constraint. That proposal passed preservation review but stayed quarantined because no known-valid witness was available. The exact Eurus2 example remains unresolved: its scaffold-removal span matched, but the model also proposed removing a compatible code-format directive using a substring with incorrect leading whitespace. Exact-span validation rejected the entire proposal and retained the original. No Eurus2 grader parity was established. No harmful edit was observed among the three accepted synthetic repairs; this panel is too small to estimate a harmful-edit rate.

The job was `/dlwh/prompt-repair-calibration-10350-v2-20261020`, attempt `/0:0`, UID `06bbd411ad38b10d`. Inference/audit took 36.14 seconds; task duration was 57.55 seconds. The 17 recorded inference requests used 31,184 prompt tokens and 3,718 completion tokens; dollar cost was not measured. The GLM 5.3 revision label identifies the observed relay binding, not verified upstream weights. Private evidence is at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/prompt-repair/calibration/2026.10.20.10350.2/`: `report.json`, `tasks.jsonl`, `inspection.json`, `attempt.txt`, and `logs.txt`. Labels are at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/prompt-repair/calibration-inputs/2026.10.20.10350.1/labels.json`. Remaining work includes correcting the Eurus2 proposal behavior and obtaining valid witnesses for sandbox-graded repairs. The frozen 10k pilot and cleaned v0 pool release have not run.

Follow-up (2026-10-20): local commit `f28dddfdff` moves public edit validation into the bounded proposal-attempt loop and adds correction requests containing the invalid proposal and public validation error. Policy revision 3 preserves compatible output-format examples. Regression coverage checks correction, exhausted retries, unchanged batch peers, and exact cache replay; optional calibration witnesses are pinned to original task hashes and use the existing sandbox grader backend. Lint and scoped types pass; the follow-up passed 112 library repair/control/source tests (one skipped), 17 focused retry/witness checks, and 406 affected tests. The four witness cases were rerun after the final assertion cleanup.

The [v3 ten-case recalibration](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fdlwh%2Fprompt-repair-calibration-10350-v3-20261020) completed model decisions, preserving both Eurus2 code-format instructions and producing a scaffold-only proposal. All three synthetic repairs matched labels and passed actual nonempty numeric positive/negative checks. The eight Eurus2/IFEval checks were infrastructure errors: their declared environment artifact had not been built. Its job exit 0 did not establish successful grader comparisons; per-task evidence retained both proposals in quarantine. Exact attempt `/0:0`, UID `ee63eb8a010d41cf`, and the inspection are retained under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/prompt-repair/calibration/2026.10.20.10350.3/`.

The missing runtime's full identity exactly matched the current registered `GRADER_PACKAGES` declaration (`dcf9294e4acb75c413121cecb5ffa9d060772b88e308a6b905d8cf57f10ee584`). The canonical builder has now published that absent worker artifact at the tasks' unchanged URL, including its hash lock, files archive, environment manifest and artifact record. Local commit `f6aa4ca1e4` also marks grader infrastructure failures as unavailable, so source/calibration completeness cannot report success when those checks never executed. The updated library repair/control/source suite passed 113 tests with one skip; lint and scoped types pass.

The [v3b targeted run](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fdlwh%2Fprompt-repair-calibration-10350-v3b-20261020) passed its actual grader gates: exact Eurus2 and stale-refusal IFEval were repaired, with positive reward 1 and nonempty negative reward 0 on both original and repaired tasks, preservation approval and unchanged re-audits. Eurus2's entire user prompt, including both compatible code-format instructions, is unchanged. All three synthetic repairs matched their expected hashes and passed the same four real numeric checks. Totals: five unchanged, five repaired, all ten reviewed. Attempt `/0:0`, UID `603e321ca855d300`, took 57.66 seconds; audit time was 39.82 seconds. Twenty provider requests used 43,017 prompt and 4,105 completion tokens. Evidence and per-task inspection are retained under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/prompt-repair/calibration/2026.10.20.10350.3b/`. One unchanged IFEval case has an ambiguous final question-generation pattern; its quarantine/unchanged judgment varied across runs. This remains an audit concern.

The [larger 64-case diagnostic](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fdlwh%2Fprompt-repair-calibration-10350-v4-20261020) saved all decisions and exited 1 because one preservation review exceeded its input budget. Outcomes were 32 unchanged, five repaired and 27 quarantined. Repair-decision statuses were 63 reviewed and one unavailable; “reviewed” includes unchanged public-audit decisions without a separate preservation review. The unavailable defragmentation task required 148,677 serialized review characters against a 128,000 limit; its original was retained.

Selection used seed 10350 and 20 tasks from one pinned shard per source: SVAMP (700 tasks in that shard), IFEval (14,973), and Eurus2 (719), plus three synthetic controls and the [exact motivating Eurus2 task](https://gist.github.com/rjpower/f796dac041e7667296af56185d99e593). These shard counts are not full-source denominators.

| Input | Unchanged | Repaired | Quarantined |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SVAMP, 20 selected | 20 | 0 | 0 |
| IFEval, 20 selected | 12 | 1 | 7 |
| Eurus2, 20 selected | 0 | 0 | 20 |
| Synthetic scaffolded SVAMP, three controls | 0 | 3 | 0 |
| Exact Eurus2 example | 0 | 1 | 0 |

All 64 saved records received AI-assisted source/contract inspection and structural checks. No harmful accepted edit was observed among the five repairs. Each accepted repair passed four actual graded checks: positive reward 1 and nonempty negative reward 0 on original and repaired versions, for 20 checks total. Each repaired task's re-audit returned unchanged. The three synthetic outputs matched canonical TaskSpec hashes fixed in the labels file before execution. Forty additional in-process numeric checks used independently derived answers and nonempty wrong answers for the 20 unchanged SVAMP tasks. Exact Eurus2 retained its entire user prompt and both code-format directives; its imported grader contains only one sample test. The repaired IFEval grader checks only lowercase. Semantic preservation was inspected separately. These results do not establish population error rates or quality across the full SVAMP, IFEval or Eurus2 datasets.

The 27 quarantines comprise 17 missing known-valid witnesses, five preservation refusals, four direct public-audit quarantine decisions without edits, and one unavailable preservation review. The inspection found a likely unwarranted IFEval quarantine (`ddbb77c6…`), unresolved instruction ambiguities, and missed mathematical content. Preservation review blocked deletion of an intentional paragraph constraint and a proposal that changed a stated unit. Static Eurus2 inspection found contracts allowing alternate answers while the imported comparator expects fixed output; no alternate-output grader probes were executed. All 20 sampled Eurus2 originals remain quarantined. One accepted exact-Eurus2 review rationale miscounted sample letters; the edit and its recorded grader results were unaffected. Per-task evidence records these findings and distinguishes unsupported validation from prompt defects.

Saved request envelopes demonstrate bounded correction on five cases: four empty-edit repair proposals and one malformed schema were corrected with distinct cache keys and two attempts each. Parsed failures carried the previous proposal and validation error; the schema failure carried the error. Proposal requests contained public messages and declared answer/tool interfaces, excluding private graders, tests, solutions and task-file contents. The leading-whitespace span failure is covered by the local regression; exact matching remains strict.

Attempt `/0:0`, UID `dd3b293cdb50b364`, took 147.2 seconds; calibration-script time was 124.46 seconds. Its 101 provider requests used 531,868 prompt and 26,000 completion tokens, including corrections, preservation reviews and re-audits. Those measurements exclude later AI-assisted inspection and the 40 extra numeric checks; dollar cost was not measured. The model revision remains an observed service binding, not a verified upstream weights pin. Private evidence is at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/prompt-repair/calibration/2026.10.20.10350.4/`: `report.json`, `tasks.jsonl`, `inspection.json`, three `source-*-inspection.json` files, `retry-observations.json`, `attempt.txt`, `logs.txt`, and `completion-audit.json`.

The requested retry, format-preservation fix, actual Eurus2/IFEval grader comparisons, targeted rerun and larger diagnostic audit are complete locally. Commits remain unpushed; the worktree is clean. Broader admission needs more witnesses, resolution of source/grader defects and a policy for large preservation inputs. The [frozen 10k pilot #10315](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10315) and [v0 pool curation/release #10314](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10314) have not run. This issue remains open.

Clef follow-up (2026-10-21): added an optional hosted decision-model filter before prompt repair, following the [service instructions](https://openathena.slack.com/archives/C0AHF5KV11Q/p1792094963618349). Enable it with `--thinking-filter-model-revision LABEL`; `--thinking-filter-keep-probability` defaults to `0.9`. It sends only public messages and declared interfaces to `/v1/systemone`. Only sufficiently high `keep` probability bypasses the editor. Uncertainty, unavailable/invalid responses, oversized requests and suspect or missing truncation metadata route to the editor. The bypass covers thinking scaffolding only; it does not establish general prompt quality. Edits still require preservation review, known-correct and known-wrong submissions graded on both versions, and an editor re-audit that proposes no further changes.

The [screening diagnostic](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fdlwh%2Fclef-thinking-screen-10350-96-20261021) covered 96 cases: eight native converted tasks from each of ten datasets, plus 16 targeted controls (14 synthetic and the exact Eurus2 original/repaired pair). Sources were SVAMP, IFEval, Eurus2, GSM8K, GPQA, Gretel text-to-SQL, APPS, Reasoning Gym, TaskTrove structured outputs and Nemotron toolcall-schema. Each native sample used seed 10350 within the first 128 successful TaskSpecs of one chosen shard, not the full source. Prediction-blind AI-assisted labels marked 16 positives (excessive incidental thinking prescriptions), 79 negatives (no such defect) and one ambiguous case. These are not human gold; all eight native positives share one Eurus2 scaffold.

At the executed `0.90` threshold, all 16 positives and the ambiguous case were routed, with 40 negatives bypassed. Post-hoc analysis at `0.70` routes the same positives and ambiguous case while bypassing 76 negatives. Of the three remaining negatives, two were false routes from model scores (worked-example reasoning and quoted thinking instructions); one 82,008-character tool-use request exceeded the 48,000-character client budget and made no model call. One positive's raw categorical answer was `keep`, but its low keep probability correctly triggered routing. Thus 16/16 is observed routing recall on this labelled panel, not a claim that every positive was classified `rewrite` or that recall generalizes. The `0.70` threshold is exploratory and was selected after inspecting this panel; `0.90` was specified before execution.

The 95 unique provider responses used 87,796 input tokens and zero generation tokens. Screening took 3.32 seconds, excluding setup, input loading and final report writing. All responses carried usage and a 16,384-token window; reported inputs were 389–9,916 tokens. Truncation was not observed. Model label `clef-orion-relay-02a-observed-2026-10-21` identifies the observed service binding, not verified upstream weights. Dollar cost and an unfiltered end-to-end baseline were not measured.

The [filter-to-editor integration diagnostic](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fdlwh%2Fclef-thinking-rewrite-10350-81-20261021) then processed the same 80 native tasks plus the exact Eurus2 original at threshold `0.70`, reusing 80 cached Clef decisions. Seventy tasks bypassed the editor; 11 were routed, including the over-budget fallback. Results were 72 unchanged and nine quarantined, with every returned TaskSpec exactly equal to its original. Quarantined originals remain in diagnostic evidence and are ineligible for acceptance. Six proposals lacked known-valid witnesses; three failed preservation approval. The exact Eurus2 proposal again tried to delete a compatible code-format directive and was blocked by its medium-confidence preservation review. The remaining two preservation refusals concerned source/grader defects. No new grader comparisons executed because all proposed edits were held before that gate. Editor requests numbered 22, using 207,035 prompt and 8,838 completion tokens; pipeline time was 62.65 seconds. This demonstrates routing and conservative retention, with no accepted live edit in this run.

Both diagnostics exited 1 because the filter recorded the one oversized request as unavailable; the integration editor reviewed that task and retained it unchanged. Screening attempt `/0:0` UID `2358515d3a994934` took 23.94 seconds; integration attempt `/0:0` UID `4ce9defb4a287398` took 81.96 seconds. Private artifacts are under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/prompt-repair/clef/2026.10.21.10350.1/`: pinned panels, `native-manifest.json`, prediction-blind labels, `inspection.json`, and `rewrite-inspection.json`; `screen/` and `rewrite/` retain reports, decisions, exact attempts and bounded logs. The integration's bundled scope string predates the optional rewrite wording fix; `rewrites.jsonl` records the actual outcomes.

The filter is opt-in. Local commit `fcdcf4bc172a0950aa51478ba9779ffe75bb8b1f` contains the pipeline, tests and usage docs; it has not been pushed. Validation: 410 affected safe tests, 152 source/filter/repair tests, and the duplicate-input calibration regression passed; lint and scoped types passed. Token accounting now deduplicates shared provider responses. This work does not establish source-wide quality, curate the frozen 10k pilot, or publish a cleaned v0 pool. Further quality validation should use new examples and more native reasoning-instruction styles before changing the default threshold.
