comments.body:
🤖
# Research

[#9626](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9626) calls `analyze_rollouts()` between evaluation and task generation, but its dummy analyzer groups every reward below 1 by a hard-coded capability ID; the reduced rollout record drops the grade and execution failure evidence needed to tell an incorrect answer from a failed run. #9626 is open and [#9638](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9638) owns the full RSI loop, so this issue can own the analysis stage without duplicating that work. The linked Google Doc redirects to sign-in from this environment, leaving its required grouping and prompt-generation rules unverified.

**Relevant code**
- [`pipeline.py#L82-L97`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9774e2cd1b4acac2b8b1524e710b217a700fcc22/experiments/post_training/baby_rsi/pipeline.py#L82-L97) — evaluation-to-analysis-to-generation call chain.
- [`dummy.py#L228-L242`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9774e2cd1b4acac2b8b1524e710b217a700fcc22/experiments/post_training/baby_rsi/dummy.py#L228-L242) — reward-only failure grouping.
- [`interfaces.py#L13-L57`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9774e2cd1b4acac2b8b1524e710b217a700fcc22/experiments/post_training/baby_rsi/interfaces.py#L13-L57) — prompt and reduced rollout contracts.
- [`contracts.py#L75-L86`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d8ac9acfd4f1425e8e6caad28fae70b904e5c5bb/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/contracts.py#L75-L86) — full grade and failure evidence.

# Proposed Fix

## Design

Implement `AnalysisEngine.analyze_failed_runs` at the #9626 artifact boundary after that PR lands. Preserve each evaluation rollout's task ID, public capability metadata, grade, and execution failure in the analysis input; retain raw task text, expected answers, verifier files, and private traces outside the generator-facing `TaskPromptSet`. Apply the evaluation's explicit pass criterion to completed, valid grades. Count grading and infrastructure failures separately so they do not become training targets. Group valid policy failures by the capability and failure categories specified in the linked document, emit stable prompt IDs and deterministic ordering, and save counts plus source rollout IDs in the private analysis artifact for audit and replay. An empty set of valid policy failures produces an empty prompt set.

## Sequence and validation

1. Rebase on #9626 and keep this PR limited to the analysis input, analyzer, and analysis artifact; leave task generation, training, and the loop coordinator to #9638 and their existing PRs.
2. Add fixture-based tests for wrong answers, partial credit at the configured threshold, successful answers, grader/runtime failures, repeated failures in one category, deterministic output, and exclusion of held-out answer text from prompts. Run the one-round Baby RSI fixture to check that the generated task path consumes the new prompts.
3. Run the touched package's default tests, `./infra/pre-commit.py --all-files --fix`, and the required PR review gate. Record the analysis artifact schema and prompt revision so a later round can reproduce the same selection.

## Open decision

Please provide the linked document's analysis section or read access before implementation. It must settle the failure taxonomy, pass criterion, prompt fields, and whether GLM synthesizes prompts; those choices change the API and tests. The deterministic grouping above is the smallest implementation consistent with the current `TaskPromptSet`, pending that specification.

issues.author: ravwojdyla-agent
issues.body:
PR #9626 adds a bounded artifact graph for the post-training recursive self-improvement (RSI) loop. The graph uses `TaskSpec`, TaskCompendium Parquet, `ShellboxRolloutEngine`, Marin artifact steps, and real grading. The policy, task generation, task filter, failure analysis, and training stages use deterministic stubs.

Replace the stubs with one small-model path that runs the full loop on Iris. The run must start from a pinned checkpoint and a held-out evaluation set. It must generate new tasks from observed failures, train new model weights, and evaluate the new checkpoint on the same held-out set.

Related open work:

- #7098: run post-training experiments from Marin
- #9612: use one rollout engine for `TaskSpec` rollouts
- #9122: define the task environment contract
- #7799: build a normalized and versioned post-training data pool
- #8089: establish the cold-start SFT recipe
- #6503: run configured evaluations and publish their results
- marin-community/MarinSkyRL#809: define the supported RL training contract
- [Post-training project](https://github.com/orgs/marin-community/projects/5): draft items for problem generation and error-mode identification

Done when:

- One versioned configuration identifies the base checkpoint, task sources, held-out evaluation set, generator, trainer, and maximum round count.
- The initial evaluation stores graded rollouts and metrics before task generation.
- Failure analysis converts failed rollouts into task prompts without copying held-out answers into training data.
- The problem generator writes verifiable `TaskSpec` records, and the task filter records accepted and rejected tasks.
- The shared rollout engine generates and grades training rollouts.
- The trainer updates real model weights and exports a checkpoint that the next evaluation can load.
- The final evaluation uses the original held-out set and records a comparison with the initial evaluation.
- Every stage records immutable inputs, outputs, and versions. A failed run can continue from completed artifacts.
- A small-model smoke run completes at least one feedback round on Iris and links its artifacts from this issue.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

[#9626](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9626) defines a bounded artifact graph, but its policy is a capability list and its analysis, generator, filter, and trainer are stubs. Its rollout records retain only four fields. [#9623](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9623) supplies the shared TaskCompendium rollout engine, and its [Qwen3-4B Iris smoke](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9612#issuecomment-5933580920) produced one optimizer step and a loadable HF export. Both PRs remain open and own the graph and rollout engine foundations.

**Relevant code**
- [`pipeline.py#L175-L280`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9774e2cd1b4acac2b8b1524e710b217a700fcc22/experiments/post_training/baby_rsi/pipeline.py#L175-L280) — bounded artifact dependencies.
- [`interfaces.py#L23-L69`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9774e2cd1b4acac2b8b1524e710b217a700fcc22/experiments/post_training/baby_rsi/interfaces.py#L23-L69) — dummy policy and reduced rollout records.
- [`dummy.py#L1-L30`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9774e2cd1b4acac2b8b1524e710b217a700fcc22/experiments/post_training/baby_rsi/dummy.py#L1-L30) — replacement boundaries.
- [`task_rollouts.py#L201-L247`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/96936d8f7762c3cea613ff2353e3bde0f656205b/experiments/post_training/task_rollouts.py#L201-L247) — working Qwen3-4B trainer configuration.
- [`skyrl.py#L212-L225`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/skyrl.py#L212-L225) — exported checkpoint and evaluation adapter.

# Proposed Fix

## Design

Extend the #9626 graph with one versioned `BabyRsiConfig`: `Qwen/Qwen3-4B@1cfa9a7` as the base policy, a pinned TaskCompendium math source with disjoint held-out IDs, a pinned generator model and prompt revision, the #9623 SkyRL trainer recipe, seed, artifact prefix, and caps of one round, 32 held-out tasks, 32 accepted new tasks, and one optimizer step. Select and freeze the held-out IDs before the baseline run. Use the same TaskSpec Parquet artifact, generation settings, and task IDs for the baseline and final evaluation; record per-task grades and aggregate pass counts. Mark a run with no baseline failures inconclusive.

Replace the in-memory `PolicyState` and reduced `RolloutBuffer` with artifact references to the policy export and full graded `RolloutData`. Add an `ArtifactSkyRLModel` input adapter so the exported `SkyRLModel.policy_export_uri` from round *n* can initialize round *n+1*; `ArtifactHfModel` currently expects a Levanter checkpoint. Keep the existing Marin artifact fingerprints and write a manifest for each stage with the config revision, input artifact identities, task/verifier versions, model revision, seed, and output paths. This lets a retry reuse completed stages while rejecting mismatched inputs.

Failure analysis should consume only public task metadata, the model response, grade, and failure category. Its output is a capability-level `TaskPrompt`; the generator must not receive the held-out Parquet, task text, expected answers, or private verifier payload. Adapt the existing [math curriculum generator](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9774e2cd1b4acac2b8b1524e710b217a700fcc22/experiments/post_training/baby_rsi/generation.py) to produce new TaskSpecs with independently checked answers. Persist every proposed task and an accept/reject decision with a reason; reject malformed or unverifiable tasks and exact or normalized duplicates of held-out and accepted training tasks. Feed accepted TaskSpecs to `ShellboxRolloutEngine`, retain its graded trajectories and failures, and pass only valid training records to the SkyRL trainer. Report the paired baseline/final results even if the score falls.

## Sequence and validation

1. Land or rebase on #9623 and #9626, then pin the exact revisions of the TaskCompendium source, generator, SkyRL runtime, and base checkpoint in one config. Keep the RSI implementation on a follow-up branch so it does not duplicate either open PR.
2. Add behavior tests for held-out answer isolation, accepted/rejected task audit rows, artifact invalidation on changed inputs, and loading the previous round's exported weights. Exercise baseline → generation → training → final evaluation with a tiny local fixture before Iris.
3. Run the one-round Qwen3-4B smoke on Iris with the proven 16-H100 topology from #9623. Publish the initial graded rollouts, filter decisions, training rollouts, optimizer step, HF export/reload evidence, final graded rollouts, and comparison here. Preserve a failed or negative result with its artifact links.

## Risks and open decision

The current [curriculum generator](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9774e2cd1b4acac2b8b1524e710b217a700fcc22/experiments/post_training/baby_rsi/README.md#L37-L64) checks a generated answer with an independent solve but can still accept a shared mistake; the smoke must keep those audit rows and grade training rollouts with TaskCompendium. Which pinned math cohort should be the held-out set? I would start with a fixed TaskTrove math subset after [#9587](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9587) lands, because it already targets TaskSpec conversion and keeps this first loop within one verifier family.

`rigging.provenance.launch_provenance` records the launching process's `sys.argv` as `command_line` (`lib/rigging/src/rigging/provenance.py`, line 123). The Marin executor writes that provenance to every artifact's `.artifact.json` (`lib/marin/src/marin/execution/artifact.py`). If a launcher receives secrets on the command line, such as `iris ... -e WANDB_API_KEY <value> -e HF_TOKEN <value>`, the raw values are stored in the bucket's artifact record and are readable by anyone with bucket access.

This was found on 2026-10-21 in the SFT-shootout parent-link artifacts under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/checkpoints/karan/arm-parent-*/.artifact.json`. Their `provenance.command_line` fields contain the `-e` arguments and their values. No values are reproduced here or elsewhere. The owner has been told and will decide on rotation.

Done when:

1. `launch_provenance` drops or masks values following `-e` or `--env` style flags, and values for names matching `*_TOKEN`, `*_KEY`, or `*_SECRET`, while retaining the flag and name. Prefer recording only secret names.
2. A one-off pass scans existing `.artifact.json` records for `-e` followed by a name ending in `TOKEN`, `KEY`, or `SECRET` under `provenance.command_line`, and rewrites records containing such values while preserving every other field.
3. Documentation identifies `iris -e` as the wrong way to pass secrets when a provenance record will be written. The `gcp-secret://` references used elsewhere do not have this problem.

comments.body:
🤖
# Research

`Provenance.capture()` copies raw `sys.argv` into `command_line`; an inherited `MARIN_PROVENANCE` payload is returned unchanged. Iris submits that JSON in the job environment, and Marin writes it into `.artifact.json`. Iris's existing argv redactor protects its CLI submission report, not these paths; malformed provenance is also logged verbatim.

**Relevant code**
- [`provenance.py#L102-L126`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/rigging/src/rigging/provenance.py#L102-L126) — raw capture.
- [`provenance.py#L167-L179`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/rigging/src/rigging/provenance.py#L167-L179) — inherited payload and log.
- [`redaction.py#L56-L93`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/redaction.py#L56-L93) — existing Iris flag parser.
- [`types.py#L754-L774`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/types.py#L754-L774) — job environment propagation.
- [`artifact.py#L364-L374`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/artifact.py#L364-L374) — record persistence.

# Proposed Fix

1. Ship capture-time containment first. Put the argv sanitizer in `rigging` and reuse it from Iris. Preserve flag and variable names, replace values for `-e`, `--env`, and Iris's `--env-vars` (including attached forms), and scrub recognized inline credentials in other arguments using the existing `rigging.redaction` primitives. Sanitize both local `sys.argv` and inherited `MARIN_PROVENANCE` before either is submitted or recorded. Stop logging malformed payload bytes. Keep `from_json` lossless for reading existing records.
2. Test with synthetic values: bare and attached flags, repeated pairs, inherited provenance, a benign argument, malformed payload logging, and the serialized Iris environment and Marin record. Update the Iris CLI help, README, and tutorial/recipe commands that currently show `-e WANDB_API_KEY "$WANDB_API_KEY"`. Document shell-based auto-injection for `HF_TOKEN` and `WANDB_API_KEY`; per-job `gcp-secret://` resolution is proposed in [#7565](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7565), not supported by the current job env path.
3. After the containment code reaches writers, run a bounded, dry-run inventory of `.artifact.json` under the reported S3 prefix, then expand by agreed prefixes. A one-off script should rewrite only `provenance.command_line`, leave every other JSON field intact, skip already-clean records, and report paths/counts without printing values. On apply, avoid plaintext backup objects and protect against concurrent writes; verify the changed field and counts with a second scan. Check object versions and other copies of `MARIN_PROVENANCE` in Iris job records before declaring remediation complete. The owner handles credential rotation.

The object rewrite needs an explicit prefix inventory and a decision on old S3 versions or backups: overwriting the current object may leave older copies readable. No bucket scan or rewrite has been run in this triage.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## Goal

Run a weight-merging loop on spare Marin compute: merge Snowball checkpoints on CPU (reserved v4 hosts in us-central2-b), screen the merges cheaply with TPU vLLM on preemptible single-host slices, and promote winners to the H100 policy evaluation. This issue tracks the project end to end.

## Pins

- Marin base `24ce375f06`
- vLLM fork `fb02daf1d7139d2adaeb0588448649591657d1e3`, tpu-inference `ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d` (head of marin-community/tpu-inference#27, stacked on #29 and #28), applied job-locally
- Evalchemy `3bb8278`, MATH500 full set, harness seed 19311
- S = `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02` @ `50fe2f488aee7730bbccc721024b35229075602e`

## Status

| Step | State |
|---|---|
| Inventory, feasibility, campaign matrix | done 2026-10-15 |
| Parents S, C, A5, M staged and sha256-verified in `gs://marin-us-central2/scratch/karan/rsi-merge/parents/` | done 2026-10-16 |
| Merge toolkit: allowlisted BF16 to F32 widening for M's router biases (branch `task/197`) | done, no PR yet |
| TPU scoring smoke test | done: TPU scores 6-7 points below H100 |
| Matched H100 control | done 2026-10-17: 0.944 |
| Quantized serving on v5e | blocked: the pinned fork rejects every quant config for GrugMoE |
| Localize the TPU gap | in progress (#10250) |
| Iteration-one merges (3 recipes) | not started, waiting on the scoring path |

## MATH500 scores for S, same model revision, same Evalchemy pin, same effective sampling

| Server | Score |
|---|---|
| H100 policy config, 2026-10-03 record | 0.950 |
| H100 policy config, 2026-10-17 | 0.944 |
| TPU v6e-8 TP8 bf16 (two runs) | 0.878, 0.882 |
| TPU v5p-8 TP4 bf16 | 0.884 |

Per item: 421 right everywhere, 39 right on both H100 runs and wrong on TPU, 12 wrong everywhere. The 39 are long solutions; 22 of them drift onto a different problem mid-solution.

## The TPU gap (#10250)

Teacher-forced logprobs on the same 10 items match the H100 within noise up to token 2047 and diverge from exactly token 2048, which is S's `sliding_window` (`global_every` 4). The gap grows to about 0.14 nat mean absolute logprob difference by 3-4k tokens.

Ruled out: truncation, thinking mode, sampling (Evalchemy strips temperature and seed, both servers run vLLM defaults), batch dependence, sharding degree and chip generation (v5p-8 TP4 scores the same), cross-request contamination, mask off-by-one (training, FA3 and the TPU kernel all keep the last W tokens including self), KV block eviction (the TPU runner keeps one full-attention cache group), per-layer window plumbing (reaches the TPU kernel unchanged; global layers get no window), KV cache dtype (bf16 on both).

Not valid controls at this pin: `grugmoe_attention_mode=dense` (never read by the vLLM model), a GPU TP8 run (GPU GrugMoE requires TP=1), the experimental batched RPA kernel (fails to compile: its SMEM schedule is sized from a reported capacity above the compiler's 1 MiB limit).

A standalone probe of the pinned ragged-paged-attention v3 kernel against its dense reference with random inputs passes 22 cases around the window boundary (error flat at bf16 noise). Random inputs spread attention over about 2048 keys, so that probe cannot see an edge or sink effect. Running now: a kernel probe with peaky scores, a BOS-like sink key and position-bucket values, and a TPU serving control with the window disabled.

Consequence for the loop: TPU vLLM cannot rank merges until this is fixed. One H100x8 MATH500 run costs about 14 minutes of box time per candidate.

## Related

- #10250 TPU sliding-window divergence
- #9400 tpu-inference pin bump and hardware checks
- #8323 Snowball TPU serving
- #7555 earlier long-context divergence on TPU
- marin-community/tpu-inference#28 custom router selections, #29 host storage release, #27 TP8 head padding (the stack every TPU run here used)
- Two Evalchemy integration gotchas found on the way: the pinned Evalchemy strips `temperature` and `seed` from requests, so the server's defaults apply; and marin's FineStore result reader expects native results JSON while Evalchemy `3bb8278` writes parquet tables, so the parent eval job reports FAILED although the child succeeded and the score is in `data/evalchemy_results/`.

## Open decisions

1. Score iteration-one merges on H100 now, or wait for the TPU fix.
2. Open a PR for the merge-toolkit change on `task/197`.
3. File the Iris autoscaler tier-blocking issue (a v6e-4 group in backoff blocks v6e-8 demand in the same zone).

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
## TPU serving defect localized: global attention layers get the sliding window

Follow-up to the seven-way comparison above. The TPU-side defect is now named and fixed by a config override; the proper fix is in tpu-inference.

**What happens.** tpu-inference registers a vLLM general plugin (`tpu_inference/layers/vllm/__init__.py`, `register_layers` -> `_register_grugmoe`). Whenever the TPU stack is present it sets `_CONFIG_REGISTRY["grug_moe"] = GrugMoeHfConfig`, replacing the vLLM fork's `GrugMoeConfig`. `GrugMoeHfConfig` (`tpu_inference/models/jax/grugmoe.py`) is a plain `PretrainedConfig` with name aliases; it never sets `layer_types`. The fork's `GrugMoeConfig` sets `layer_types` from `grug_moe_layer_types(num_layers, global_every)`. Plugins load in `EngineArgs.__post_init__`, before the model config is built, so on TPU `hf_text_config.layer_types` is `None`. vLLM then sets `cache_config.sliding_window = 2048` (arg_utils: "only set CacheConfig.sliding_window if the model is all sliding window"), and the fork's GrugMoE model, which passes `per_layer_sliding_window=None` for its 7 global layers (3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, 25 of 26), gets 2048 for them through the `Attention.__init__` fallback. A static trace of the TPU engine shows all 26 layers at `sliding_window=2048`. On H100 the plugin is absent, the fork config is used, and the engine builds 4 KV cache groups with the global layers unwindowed. The fork model derives its own layer pattern from `global_every`, so nothing crashes; the window is just applied to the wrong layers.

**Verification.** Passing `--hf-overrides '{"layer_types": [...]}'` (the fork's list: `full_attention` at 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, 25, `sliding_attention` elsewhere) changes the trace to 7 layers at `None` and 19 at 2048, with 4 KV cache groups. Teacher-forced probe (same 10 MATH500 items, 35,801 positions) against the exact-window eager reference, mean |delta logprob|:

| positions | TPU, override | TPU, default | H100 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-2048 | 0.015-0.018 | 0.015-0.018 | 0.014-0.016 |
| 2048-2304 | 0.013-0.016 | 0.023-0.038 | 0.012-0.014 |
| 2304-3072 | 0.015-0.017 | 0.054-0.080 | 0.014-0.016 |
| 3072+ | 0.012-0.015 | 0.132-0.142 | 0.011-0.014 |

TPU with the override vs H100 directly: 0.011-0.017 at every position. MATH500 with the override (Evalchemy 3bb8278, seed 19311, same settings as the TPU runs above): **0.940** (470/500, 500 generated and scored, 1421 s), against 0.878-0.884 for TPU without it and 0.944 / 0.950 for the two H100 runs. The gap is closed.

**Fix.** Proper fix is in tpu-inference: `GrugMoeHfConfig` should set `layer_types` the same way the fork does, or the plugin should not replace a registry entry the fork already provides. tpu-inference `main` at 340444337772 (2026-10-19) still has the overwrite. Until then, TPU serving of any GrugMoE checkpoint whose `config.json` lacks `layer_types` needs the override above. Pins: vLLM fork fb02daf, tpu-inference ae387b8, Step12 @50fe2f488aee.

🤖
# Research

At 18:16–18:19 UTC, the hub still marked `cw-rno2a` unreachable with last contact at 17:14:22. The peer controller Service endpoint was Ready and `/health` returned 200 inside the cluster, but a direct controller status RPC timed out; hub heartbeat logs report repeated `Request timed out`. `FederationPeer.probe()` keeps the last backend snapshot after a failed probe, so `ListPeers` forwards stale free capacity and queued-job status says it is waiting for capacity without checking peer reachability.

**Relevant code**
- [`peer.py#L192-L215`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/federation/peer.py#L192-L215) — probe failure retains backends
- [`manager.py#L476-L486`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/federation/manager.py#L476-L486) — peer summary forwards snapshot
- [`service.py#L759-L773`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/service.py#L759-L773) — queued-job reason omits reachability

# Proposed Fix

`ListBackends` times out → the hub marks the peer unreachable → pinned jobs remain queued, but their status still says “report free capacity.” Report the unreachable peer in detail and list job status, and omit stale availability values from unreachable `ListPeers` summaries while retaining last-known backend shapes for routing. For the live incident, isolate the peer's `ListBackends` timeout (including controller load and concurrent finelog send failures), restore that RPC through an approved targeted operation, then verify contact and availability timestamps advance and queued jobs start. No cluster operation has been changed.

Jobs that failed or were killed on cw-rno2a in the window: dml 58, bizon 29, benfeuer 26, karan 4, larry 4, exedev 2, eczech 1. Not all of these were caused by the outage.
- **Controller-side changes:** none visible from the marin controller's DB or ListPeers, apart from the H100 total dropping from 512 to 504. I can't see whether the cw-rno2a controller was restarted.

issues.body:
Add NVIDIA's [Skill2Env](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env) to the RL Data Atlas with a reproducible assessment that helps people decide whether to use the tasks. This issue tracks registration, conversion, validation, and publication. Training integration and upstream grader repair remain separate work.

Current status (2026-10-21): catalog registration merged in #10120 and Harbor Hub acquisition merged in #10198. The inventory entry is `Harbor Hub:skill2env`, pinned to the 7,496-task release, version 1.0.1 / revision 2, at `sha256:bef4f739bde8d865af04c04a2cb1c84ecad83b52dd558f4d582dd46c7933666c`. Live Atlas publication has not been verified.

#10154 is open for review at `8c9be40510` and adds conversion for QUICK inspection through the existing task-curation interfaces. It retains native task files, private tests and reference solutions, and defines grading through the unchanged native test script with the arithmetic mean of its reward components. Actor and verifier images remain unresolved Docker build contexts: QUICK can produce TaskSpecs for inspection, but SAMPLE/FULL execution is not ready. The earlier implementation in #9632 is superseded.

Validation so far:

- The full-release QUICK driver at `5078b1e56a` processed all 7,496 tasks in 75 batches of at most 100: 7,423 TaskSpecs, 67 `native_outputs` exclusions, and 6 `native_workspace` exclusions. All batches completed and their output archives were uploaded and hash-checked. This establishes conversion coverage, not executable-task quality.
- Static inspection of all 73 exclusions found 41 candidates for directory capture, 22 filesystem-metadata limitations, 5 live-process limitations, and 5 cases requiring startup validation. Candidate status does not establish grading equivalence.
- At `8c9be40510`, two digest-pinned candidates now convert: `task_c-memory_qi67nu17` captures `/workspace` and `/root/.claude/memory`; `task_gws-sheets-append_njhq0ebv` captures `/work` and `/var/lib/gws-local`. The unchanged native verifier and converted grading path returned identical components in all ten controls: initial state, reference solution, modified state, deleted state, and empty submission for each task. Both reference solutions scored 1.0; negative controls reduced rewards as expected.
- These ten controls used isolated, network-disabled host-Python sandboxes and the real runtime file-capture/grading interfaces. The original Docker images were not built. Other exclusions remain: 39 file-capture candidates still need validation, plus the 22 metadata, 5 live-process, and 5 startup cases. The full-release QUICK driver has not been rerun after these two exceptions.
- All 14 focused conversion and fixture-grading tests and mechanical lint pass at `8c9be40510`. The broader affected suite is left to CI; no new independent review has run on this checkpoint. The independent review of `5078b1e56a` found no actionable issues.
- Image resolution, native-container grading, quality reviews, and difficulty runs remain unfinished. No model calls were made for this conversion validation.

Remote evidence: Iris job `/exedev/skill2env-quick-batches-20261021`, recipe revision 8. Batch manifests, output archives, logs, and `result.json` are under `gs://marin-us-central2/tmp/ttl=7d/skill2env-quick-batches-20261021`. The original 7,496 archives remain cached under `gs://marin-us-central2/tmp/ttl=7d/skill2env-hub-cache-20261021`; subsequent checks can reuse them. These paths have a seven-day retention policy. The case-by-case exclusion assessment and ten-control result JSON are retained locally in `/tmp/10154-all-evidence/`.

Remaining work:

- [x] Merge the pinned catalog declaration (#10120).
- [x] Merge Harbor Hub acquisition (#10198).
- [ ] Review and merge QUICK conversion (#10154).
- [ ] Build and pin actor/verifier images, configure native resource limits, and validate preservation of native grading behavior on a varied bounded sample. Keep unsupported execution contracts explicit.
- [ ] Run a bounded SAMPLE campaign under the current workflow and inspect execution, grading controls, task quality, and model difficulty results. Document defects, exclusions, and assessment limits.
- [ ] Publish the inventory through a curation campaign and verify the live Atlas source entry. Inventory publication does not require executing Skill2Env.
- [ ] Publish and verify the resulting assessment and evidence in Atlas, then close this intake issue.

The earlier sampled investigation and verifier-defect reproduction below remain evidence for follow-up validation, not a completed assessment under the current curation workflow. Historical ratings, eligibility rules, runtime choices, and deployment procedures are not current completion requirements. The official release and grader remain unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Earlier 100-task conversion validation</summary>

Validation so far:

- The complete QUICK driver on a deliberately varied sample of 100 real tasks across 80 skill-name groups produced 99 TaskSpecs, one expected rejection, and no unexpected failures at `5078b1e56a`. The run used one CPU worker on reserved TRC capacity through Iris; captured manifests and Parquet outputs were retrieved and checked, including TaskSpec readback. This is not an estimate of release-wide coverage.
- The rejected `task_winui-app_exphg7he` requires a running process and a live socket outside `/workspace`. It remains explicitly unsupported by this adapter; copying files alone would not preserve its grading contract.
- All 14 focused conversion and fixture-grading tests and mechanical lint pass at `5078b1e56a`. GitHub review findings were addressed, including filtering stale cached archives against the current acquisition manifest. An independent review of that commit found no actionable issues.
- These checks do not establish native container grading equivalence. No full-release conversion, image build, native container grading, quality review, difficulty run, or model call was performed for the current conversion PR.

Remote validation evidence: Iris job `/exedev/skill2env-quick100-20261021-r2`, recipe revision 8, completed successfully on 2026-10-21. The driver took about 17 seconds with peak RSS about 794 MiB. Captured output archive SHA-256: `c9b7727869de36bde4091efc7612ad2075c9ef914986fa984991faa9097a7a7d`. Iris retains the remote archive for seven days; a downloaded copy, driver log, selection, manifest, and Parquet outputs are retained locally. This validates QUICK conversion only, not task execution or grading.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Historical investigation and superseded implementation plan (before #10120)</summary>

The record below is preserved for its evaluation evidence and implementation history. Status statements, integration questions, and checklists in this section refer to the former #9632 approach and are superseded by the current status above.

Add NVIDIA's [Skill2Env](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env) to the [RL Data Atlas](https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/fb11c931-5861-4878-8bb5-a964d652b45f/) with an assessment that helps people decide whether to use the tasks. This issue tracks dataset intake, validation and publication. Training integration and repairing the dataset's grader are separate work.

The target is the official [Harbor Hub release](https://hub.harborframework.com/datasets/skill2env/skill2env), revision 2, containing 7,496 tasks. Harbor shows the tags `latest` and `v1.0`; the same release's version field is `1.0.1`. These labels refer to the same content. The paper's private S2EBench evaluation set is separate.

Current status: implementation and sampled validation are prepared in PR #9632, now ready for review. The proposed Atlas rating is "Some issues" because one task's grader was shown to reject valid tests. This rating is not yet published. The official release and its grader remain unchanged; the investigation used two temporary copies with modified reference answers.

The intake can finish with a documented "Some issues" rating. Existing Atlas policy permits the standard Small/Large/Hosted model difficulty comparison only for sources rated "Good", so no difficulty comparison was launched. That is an eligibility decision, not an estimate that these tasks are easy or hard. The three-task quality sample does not establish quality across the full dataset.

Evaluation scope: reported rewards come from the released executable graders. The release also includes written rubrics; the paper's additional LLM rubric-scoring layer was not run or validated here ([§§3.2.2 and 4.2](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2609.reinforcing-agents-collective-skills.pdf)). Atlas's GLM-5.3 quality audit separately reviews tasks and graders and does not contribute to those rewards.

The PR contains the implementation and concise design rationale. The evidence and integration review questions below support the assessment. The author has marked the PR ready; Ben's Atlas integration review is still pending. The proposed sequence is review, merge, publish, then verify the live entry; this issue stays open through that verification.

### Integration questions for review

- Catalog design: add checked-in Harbor release registrations as an extension to merged #9518. To assess a newer release, a contributor would update the registration through a Marin PR. Atlas refresh would read that registration; it would not automatically switch releases. Evaluation jobs download tasks separately.
- Runtime dependency: retain the review runner's existing MarinSkyRL result adapter and checkout metadata. The catalog entry needs no training registration, but the runner still has this dependency. Review whether to keep it or separate the Harbor runner from MarinSkyRL before landing.
- Agent setup: use Atlas's Terminus-2 with checksum-pinned tools installed offline, preserving the tasks' network restrictions and resource limits. The paper used Pi; these measurements evaluate the Atlas setup.
- Evaluation budget: the sample used a 50-turn limit inherited from Atlas's example configuration. Two of three attempts reached that limit before signaling completion. Review whether this budget is sufficient for initial intake or whether a larger-budget follow-up is needed.
- Scores: preserve all native reward components from the released executable graders, report their arithmetic mean, and count a full pass only when every component reaches one within numerical tolerance. The paper's additional LLM rubric reward was not run. Atlas's separate LLM quality audit does not contribute to these scores.
- Shared tooling: keep the review-output validation, provenance, evidence-retention and provider-call fixes here, or split them into prerequisite PRs.
- Assessment scope: accept the seeded three-task sample as initial intake evidence. It does not establish quality or difficulty across all 7,496 tasks.

Done when:

- [x] Identify the official release and record its task count, source links and license scope in the proposed registration.
- [x] Run the sampled quality review and preserve the original solver, grader and review evidence.
- [x] Assess eligibility for the standard difficulty comparison; currently ineligible under the "Good"-only rule.
- [ ] Review and merge #9632.
- [ ] Reconcile the currently deployed Atlas source with Ben and agree on who will publish the update.
- [ ] Publish and verify the source entry, dated assessment and grading-problem record in Atlas, then close this intake issue.

<details>
<summary>Evaluation results, diagnostic reproduction and evidence identifiers</summary>

The official dataset accompanies [Reinforcing Agents with Collective Skills](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2609.reinforcing-agents-collective-skills). The registered release digest is `sha256:bef4f739bde8d865af04c04a2cb1c84ecad83b52dd558f4d582dd46c7933666c`. Project-owned code is Apache-2.0; third-party task assets retain their own terms.

Sampled evaluation:

Three tasks were selected with seed 42 from all 7,496 pinned release tasks. Every reference-solution reward component was 1 and every no-op component was 0. Task checksums match across those controls and the original GLM-5.3 attempts. All three model attempts reached the native grader without an execution exception; none achieved a full pass.

| Sampled task | Mean component reward | Agent outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ai-seo | 0.93 | Declared completion |
| api-design-reviewer | 0.00 | Used all 50 turns; did not declare completion |
| property-based-testing | 0.25 | Used all 50 turns; did not declare completion |

Scores describe performance within a 50-turn budget. We have not tested whether additional turns improve the two unfinished attempts.

The solver used Terminus-2, GLM-5.3 on Together, Low reasoning effort, and 65,536-total/16,384-output token limits. The Atlas quality-review panel uses GLM-5.3 for three judgments per task and task/source syntheses. All 555 trace-section reviews and 16 original records pass content, schema, reference and evidence-hash checks. The 246 original native artifact files remain byte-identical.

Grader diagnostic:

The task `task_property-based-testing_2kbxlnww` asks the agent to write property tests for a software-version comparison API. A separate diagnostic checked whether its grader wrongly penalizes valid self-comparison tests. Harbor's "oracle agent" runs the supplied reference solution; it is not another model.

The task was pinned at digest `c193f032e03538d875efd6a54026a39621329c2bd88614dab0160b256ed8b4a7`, using official Harbor runner commit `bf991e490394ef9c3250a6db2bc5cbda903cb4c3`. These identifiers make the diagnostic reproducible.

| Reference answer used | Mean native reward | Reference tests | Native mutation result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Authors' original answer | 1.00 | 11 pass | 12/12 killed |
| Same answer with direct self-comparison tests | 0.25 | 12 pass | Skipped by static gate |
| Same tests expressed through a variable alias | 1.00 | 12 pass | 12/12 killed |

To reproduce in a temporary copy, append this property to the reference `solution/test_properties.py`, then run the unchanged native grader through Harbor's oracle agent:

```python
@CI_SETTINGS
@example(Version(1, 2, 3))
@given(valid_versions)
def test_version_reflexivity(version):
    assert version == version
    assert version <= version
    assert version >= version
```

For the equivalent passing control, assign `same_version = version` inside the function and use `same_version` as each comparison's left operand. The grader's `is_self_comparison` compares operand syntax trees; its `no_self_comparison` gate blocks mutation testing for the direct form. The documented task contract does not prohibit valid reflexivity properties on overloaded comparisons.

Only `solution/test_properties.py` in the two temporary diagnostic copies changed. The official release, the grader and the original evaluation artifacts are preserved. All three diagnostic trials completed without an execution exception. They do not replace the original GLM score or establish whether its answer would pass the mutation threshold.

This grading defect supports the prepared "Some issues" assessment. A separate review-panel allegation of leaked SEO helpers was false: the saved trajectory shows the solver creating those helpers. The supplemental review retains the original opinions and replaces their source-level conclusion with the confirmed grading finding. Editable API verifier imports remain a separate concern without a demonstrated exploit.

Evidence and corrections:

Diagnostic job: `/exedev/skill2env-reflexivity-diagnostic-20261002-145621`. Verified diagnostic archive SHA-256: `356b88a8d0c7da1258fbdd669f63d2592991530509571539d90cadc40535a8bb`. Supplemental review SHA-256: `d27b01d25fd27933a1d25a085e65d89b4209afe778f32261a133f3e83c4de79e`.

Independent code review found two problems in the Atlas contribution: omitted trajectory files during publication, and failure to retire the final Harbor registration. Both were fixed in 8df5a15087. These fixes change Atlas tooling, not the Skill2Env grader. A publisher check now retains all nine referenced Harbor summarization files that were missing.

Eight epoch review dates were repaired using native completion timestamps and matching provider-response creation timestamps. The 573 epoch evidence-retrieval references now record their October 2 hash reverification; their original retrieval times are unknown. Original grades, judge opinions and source artifacts remain preserved. No model or native solver runs were repeated for these metadata corrections.

Corrected primary collection SHA-256: `25028bccfca5c246390665e73d8f5cc22a4c6b84a7ea85f4e15169483f7b2da1`. Original collection SHA-256: `e1c4b0befca4292ac8b0afff16a83c29c08278bf627cf81d769e25002b4545e6`. The corrected collection includes the original collection and correction manifests. Supplemental evidence distinguishes the full 7,496-task release from the runner's three staged tasks.

Publication:

Evidence and the publication plan are retained locally; neither the source nor its rating is live in Atlas. Deployed applet revision 58 contains 9,668 more bytes than the merged package (195,096 versus 185,428), although all seven frontend assets match. Obtain and reconcile its deployed manifest/backend source before replacing the applet.

On publication, add the confirmed grading defect to the source's review pool and `catalog_verifier_issues`. Closing this intake issue does not resolve that defect. Clearing its Atlas flag would require a validated fix and fresh review as separate follow-up work.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Implementation validation</summary>

Implementation validation before the Loom follow-up:

All 61 affected local tests and lint passed at `8df5a15087`. Its 17 applicable CI checks passed, including Marina's database suite; 12 were skipped. The publisher check retains all nine previously omitted referenced trajectory files. Backend-factory, migration and browser execution were not validated locally.

At `cc560d56eb`, documentation lint, an isolated Atlas-page build and the applicable GitHub CI checks passed. The local full-site documentation build failed on `ignore_init_summary` on both this branch and base `3ee6cc3e05`.

The Loom follow-up declares the serialized reward schema with `TypedDict` and marks intentionally unused test-callback arguments. It preserves reward calculation and the JSON fields. The nine directly affected local review tests, required lint and focused type check pass. All 17 applicable CI checks pass at `287291cbb4`, including Marina's database suite. The local affected-test runner requires at least two workers, so the focused tests ran serially with the complete default marker exclusions.

The PR retains concise rationale for the Harbor origin, release pinning, retained runtime dependency, scoring, evaluation limits, Harbor logging options, HTTP client identity and Qwen documentation correction. Longer validation details and the review questions live here.

</details>


</details>

[PR #9518](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9518) is the open Atlas dependency; I found no separate Skill2Env PR. Its catalog refresh reads only MarinSkyRL and Task Trove, while the native review runner accepts Harbor directories but requires MarinSkyRL provenance during generation and publication. The [official Harbor release](https://hub.harborframework.com/datasets/skill2env/skill2env) supplies task directories with `tests/test.sh`, `tests/rubric.md`, and `solution/solve.sh`; the [Skill2Env repository](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env#license) licenses project-owned code under Apache-2.0 and records separate terms for third-party skill material.

**Relevant code**
- [`catalog.py#L531`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cb91eb230b46ad188cb14b23f8c6fecdca4927ae/infra/marina/applets/rl_data_catalog/server/catalog.py#L531) — Task Trove source snapshot.

- [`make_review.py#L900`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cb91eb230b46ad188cb14b23f8c6fecdca4927ae/experiments/rl_data_reviews/make_review.py#L900) — Harbor sampling with mandatory MarinSkyRL checkout.
- [`publish_review.py#L118`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cb91eb230b46ad188cb14b23f8c6fecdca4927ae/experiments/rl_data_reviews/publish_review.py#L118) — publisher rejects missing MarinSkyRL commit.

# Skill2Env Atlas contribution

## Design

Create `agent/YYYYMMDD-fix-9630` from the latest #9518 head and open a separate PR against that branch. Register one `Skill2Env:skill2env` source row from a pinned Harbor package release, with the package version or digest, exact task count and count method, source and verifier provenance, links to the official Hub and repository, and license information supported by the released package and its source inventory. Resolve the immutable package identifier and enumerate task IDs before coding the row; do not use `latest` or infer a corpus-wide Apache-2.0 license from the code license. Catalog refresh should retain the pinned row without downloading task archives or silently advancing it.

Extend the Atlas origin list, public table and details, and refresh status for Skill2Env. Use the existing source/review tables so changed data or verifier revisions make prior ratings historical. Adapt the Harbor review route and schema to record its actual Harbor checkout, task bytes, and verifier implementation without requiring unrelated MarinSkyRL source provenance. Keep the native `tests/test.sh` result distinct from the qualitative rubric and the three independent reviewer judgments; preserve solver trajectory, verifier output, judge responses, sample IDs, seed, and dated source synthesis through publication.

Run the standard seeded quality sample against the pinned Harbor tasks and publish its rating and evidence. If it is Good, run the same task IDs through the Atlas Small (Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct), Large (Qwen3.5-122B-A10B), and Hosted (GLM-5.3) arms under the current protocol enforced by `app.py`; use its judge-verifier variant only if the native verifier calls a model. Record checkpoint identities, generation settings, per-arm solved/verified/attempted counts, and infrastructure failures separately. Publish difficulty only when the protocol matches and the source review remains current. Link the dated Atlas review and dependent implementation PR here.

## Validation and risk

Test the pinned count and links, refresh idempotence, revision-based staleness, Harbor-only provenance and publication, and public filtering. Validate the applet and inspect the public page after publication. Native Harbor execution needs a Docker-capable environment; the first sampled run must establish that the released package and its verifier work before any model comparison. Keep failed executions as evidence and out of solve-rate denominators until their status is resolved.

## Open question

Does the Hub expose an immutable package digest and task-level license metadata for this release? If it exposes only a version tag, archive a task-ID and file-hash manifest with the review so the counted and executed populations can be checked later.

Track biology evaluation coverage, tooling, and results for reference models and Snowball.

[Biology evaluations catalog](https://openathena.ai/bio-evals/) · [Catalog source](https://github.com/Open-Athena/bio-evals)

**Living summary — updated October 21, 2026.** Detailed evidence is linked from each result.

### Current results

| Model / benchmark | Result | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Snowball v0.1 Smartie Step14 / BixBench corrections v3 / Pi 1.3.0 | **19/205 (9.3%)**; all scored, only 48 nonempty submissions | [Result and reviewed trace audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6300963037) |
| Snowball v0.1 / BiomniBench-DA / Pi 0.87.0 | **4.24/100 mean rubric score**; 12/50 nonempty submissions | [Result and reviewed audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6297505720) |
| GLM-5.3 / MMLU biology | **462/554**; 81.79% mean subject accuracy, 83.39% pooled | [Run and subject results](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/glm53-mmlu-biology-full-20260918-191647) (Marina access) |
| GLM-5.3 / BixBench CLI v1.5 / Terminus-2 | **101/187 graded (54.01%)**; 18/205 ungraded | [Baseline and limitations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667) |
| GLM-5.3 / BixBench-Verified-50 / Terminus-2 | **42/49 graded (85.71%)**; 1/50 ungraded; saved-answer regrade | [Regrade and provenance](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180#issuecomment-5766684283) |
| GLM-5.3 / BixBench-Verified-50 / Pi 0.87.0 | **39/46 graded (84.78%)**; 4/50 ungraded | [Run investigation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6086246928) |

These are **not controlled model comparisons**: benchmark variants, agents, judges, budgets, and grading policies differ. Missing submissions scored zero in both Snowball runs; the GLM rows separately report ungraded outcomes.

### Current findings

Snowball’s BixBench failures are dominated by **156 missing answer files**, plus one empty submission. Traces show answers left in chat, simulated execution without real tool calls, repetition, and specific analysis mistakes. Compaction count showed little association with missing files. BFCL also had **55/123 missing submissions**; four inspected examples show related submission/tool-use failures beyond biology, without establishing one shared cause. No scores were changed.

BiomniBench-DA likewise had **38/50 missing submissions**; the 12 submitted tasks averaged 17.67/100. Its overall 4.24/100 is a rubric-score mean, not accuracy. This supplementary evaluation used five input variants and a replacement judge/scorer; it does not change the release aggregate or provide a matched reference-model comparison. [Protocol and limitations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6297505720).

[Selected HF traces](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples) show recurring simulated execution, chat-only answers, and repetitive output-limit failures across BiomniBench-DA, BixBench, and BFCL. BiomniBench also has wrong-path and rejected-write examples. These support general execution/submission problems without establishing a shared cause; [the comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6297505720) records the examples and differing Pi versions.

🤖 BixBench CLI development check: the explicit 10 GiB retry ran through the agent phase, but produced no scored answer. The initial attempt had been blocked before model inference because the task's default 20 GB disk request exceeded the Daytona account's 10 GB per-sandbox cap.

The retry used `environment.override_storage_mb: 10240`, following a [previous Harbor canary that hit the same limit](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/75#issuecomment-5461786985). Development outcome:

- Sandbox setup completed. The agent ran for its original 3,600-second budget without creating `/workspace/answer.txt`.
- BixBench's unchanged verifier returns without writing a reward when the answer file is missing. Harbor recorded `RewardFileNotFoundError`; no Together judge decision was produced. The canonical record reports **1 attempted, 0 scored**. This is not a judged incorrect answer or a benchmark accuracy estimate.
- The end-of-agent filesystem diagnostic reported **25.7 MiB used and 9.97 GiB available** in the 10 GiB allocation. No disk-exhaustion failure was observed. This is a final filesystem reading, not peak usage or the base image's total size, and it does not establish that every capsule fits.

Protocol:

- CLI adaptation, registry `bixbench-cli@1.5`, [task revision `711ff277`](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-datasets/tree/711ff277ae6b9e3950d19b40bc3e5aeb96e62b73/datasets/bixbench-cli). One development task, `bix-1-q1`, excluded from the subsequent five-question pilot. The complete registry snapshot has 205 questions.

Use the [September evaluation policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9193): 32,768 input tokens, 8,192 output tokens, and the default enabled summarization.
- Together `openai/gpt-oss-120b` verifier with BixBench's original grading prompt and Boolean response schema. Four basic live checks passed: exact and equivalent numeric answers accepted; wrong and empty answers rejected. This checks grader integration, not broad judge accuracy.
- The original base image is ARM-only. Use the [adapter author's AMD64 replacement](https://github.com/Future-House/BixBench/issues/41#issuecomment-4340332343), pinned to `sha256:485e5c776422fece8cb98addba593ea188c8a97162807a91d2a0e350522407b7`, with capsule data pinned to Hugging Face revision `f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a`.

The five-question pilot has not been launched. Before expanding, review the no-answer timeout behavior and complete a native verifier check that reaches the judge. The current failure remains in the record; it must not disappear from attempted coverage. This exploratory CLI protocol should be reported separately from the original notebook-based BixBench leaderboard and from Marin's canonical benchmark suite.

comments.body:
🤖 The five-question GLM-5.3 BixBench CLI pilot completed with an answer from every task. The original verifier scored three answers: one correct, two incorrect, and two unscored because structured JSON generation exhausted the judge's token limit. The incomplete original run retains no aggregate metric.

A separate, uniform regrade of the same five saved answers added an explicit JSON-schema instruction to the judge. It produced one correct and four incorrect results, with no JSON errors; the three previously valid grades stayed unchanged. This is a five-question integration pilot with a disclosed judge-prompt variation, not a full-benchmark accuracy estimate. The original answers, trajectories, and scores were preserved.

The format repair is in [Harbor commit `97037f79`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/97037f793efaae22e22da5b89bc9604d2e40e800). It preserves the comparison prompt, Boolean schema, judge model, and 1,024-token cap. Lint and formatting passed. The branch has no PR yet; existing registry snapshots still require regenerated or explicitly patched tasks.

Error review:

- `bix-11-q2`: 88/249 fungal trees exceed the treeness threshold, giving 35.34%, versus the reference's 35%. The regrader rejected the difference. This is a likely precision-related false negative; no score has been changed. The pinned question specifies no rounding rule, and its archive contains no reference notebook.
- `bix-52-q2`: the agent used pooled CpGs / genome length. The [reference capsule](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-4dceea58-7d66-4576-bfc6-88c026d5b7a9.zip) groups only chromosomes containing retained CpGs (notebook cells 11 and 39). Averaging those 20 chromosome densities yields 1.1283e-7, inside the reference interval. The notebook confirms the chromosome selection; the mean was recomputed from the saved table.
- `bix-28-q1`: the final analysis substituted raw terminal branch lengths and species-level medians for the [PhyKIT long-branch statistic](https://jlsteenwyk.com/PhyKIT/reference/commands/long_branch_score.html). The reference p-value has not been independently reproduced; its archive also contains no reference notebook.
- `bix-6-q7`: the agent used a top-1% replicate intersection, then mistook its own intermediate enrichment CSV for supplied results. The [reference notebook](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-f4dcda89-678d-403d-b155-1483d0071765.zip), cells 28–30, instead takes the minimum replicate P-value, selects values below 0.05, maps RefSeq IDs to symbols, and runs Reactome enrichment against measured genes. It reports “cGMP effects” with raw P ≈ 0.000024 and adjusted P ≈ 0.0327. These are saved reference outputs, not a fresh rerun.
- `bix-18-q2`: the mean swarming area was correctly rounded to 82,000.

Six additional fixed judge diagnostics accepted `35.0%` as equivalent to `35%`, rejected `45%`, and classified one value inside and one outside the CpG reference interval correctly. The exact-percent and higher-precision examples returned provider server errors, so this check did not resolve the rounding concern. No tolerance or solver setting was retuned.

The [previously documented protocol](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5736346928) and explicit environment overrides were retained. All five pilot agents submitted within their original time limits, with no observed disk exhaustion. The full 205-question run remains pending a decision on numerical grading; original scores will remain intact.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 GLM-5.3 completed 205 fresh BixBench CLI attempts: **101 correct / 187 graded (54.01%)**, with **18 ungraded**. Grading coverage is **91.22%**. Marin's 95% interval accounting for ungraded items is **43.79–63.43%**; 54.01% is the accuracy among graded questions.

All 177 valid native grades were retained. Eleven saved answers whose verifier calls failed with HTTP 503 received one additional grading attempt each, with the original SDK retry policy. Ten obtained grades (eight correct, two incorrect); one still failed with a provider error. No solver was rerun or answer edited. The original run and its artifacts remain preserved.

The 18 ungraded outcomes are:

- 14 missing answer/reward files following the 3,600-second agent limit.
- Two sandbox processes killed with exit 137 (`TmuxBatchProtocolError`); the cause is unconfirmed.
- One Daytona HTTP 502 gateway failure.
- One unresolved judge server error (`bix-10-q2`).

Three other trials reported `AgentTimeoutError` but produced valid verifier results; those grades remain included. Missing grades are excluded from the accuracy denominator and shown separately. The original private exporter mistakenly required 100% grading coverage; its incomplete record is preserved. The derived result applies [Marin's standard 90% completion gate](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a28c29a008a3ddc1a62fb348c52217a4429e5491/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py), consistent with the reporting policy in #9193. The original sample export displayed missing rewards as incorrect; the derived archive preserves all 18 as ungraded.

Protocol: `bixbench-cli@1.5`, Harbor `7b18505a56e5624f55887e3b20f4de452f698a7a`, task revision `711ff277ae6b9e3950d19b40bc3e5aeb96e62b73`, Terminus-2, 16 concurrent trials, 32,768 input / 8,192 output tokens, default summarization, and 3,600-second agent / 600-second verifier limits. The judge was Together `openai/gpt-oss-120b` with the original comparison prompt and 1,024-token cap. The [explicit JSON-schema repair](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/97037f793efaae22e22da5b89bc9604d2e40e800) applied to every task; numerical tolerances were unchanged. The [previously documented](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5742640265) 10 GiB disk override, pinned AMD64 image, and task-manifest hash were retained.

Validation checked all 205 task identities, sample counts against aggregate scores, all retained native grades, and the eleven selected recovery cases. Two archived trajectories were also compared byte-for-byte through the dashboard API. This establishes an exploratory CLI baseline; ID/OOD status remains unassigned. The replacement judge, missing grades, known precision caveat from the pilot, and unavailable exact serving weights revision limit comparisons with other protocols. Next: review full-run scientific errors and compare future models under this same recorded protocol.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 Reviewed all 86 recorded incorrect answers and all 18 ungraded outcomes from the [completed BixBench CLI baseline](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667), using saved answers/trajectories and the archived reference notebooks where available. No solver or judge calls were rerun. The result remains **101/187 correct (54.01%), with 18/205 ungraded**.

Each incorrect answer has a primary review category:

| Category | Questions | Interpretation |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Observed analysis or protocol divergence | 54 | Identified differences in statistic, counting unit, filtering, cohort, model or enrichment workflow. Some choices are underspecified in the question; these are not all established scientific mistakes. |
| Answer precision or representation review | 11 | Submitted values may differ through rounding or units; this does not establish 11 false negatives. |
| Question or reference adjudication | 7 | Contradictory targets, unclear counting/aggregation, or unresolved reference-data provenance. |
| Numerical or pipeline mismatch unresolved | 14 | Insufficient evidence to isolate the cause without reconstructing more of the reference pipeline. |

The review ledger records a finding, confidence level, trace evidence and pinned reference capsule for each of the 104 nonpassing outcomes. Original trajectories remain in the existing evaluation archive; the detailed review ledger is retained with the private evaluation handoff. The categories above are follow-up queues, not a corrected accuracy estimate.

Concrete analysis findings:

- `bix-61-q1`: reported **4,818 discarded read pairs across two samples**. The MDR trimming log reconstructs the reference's **344,895 discarded individual reads** exactly: 334,988 forward-only survivors + 1,075 reverse-only survivors + 2 × 4,416 fully dropped pairs. Both the counting unit and sample scope changed.
- `bix-28-q4` and `bix-45-q5`: substituted a different statistic. The former used terminal-branch means grouped by species instead of per-tree long-branch scores; the latter used BUSCO score/cutoff instead of [PhyKIT relative composition variability](https://jlsteenwyk.com/PhyKIT/tutorials/pages/01-summarizing-information-content.html).
- `bix-16-q1/q3`: raw Chronos scores were used without the reference's sign reversal. `bix-20-q1/q3`: unclassified variants entered the denominator; the reference excludes them, giving 13/14 and 35/37. These differences are visible in the [essentiality reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-bda54b38-9b49-4009-aad6-d5f52675438a.zip), cell 34, and [variant reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-2ccdbe37-0a92-47b5-9bab-fa8a8c470799.zip), cell 18.
- RNA-seq failures repeatedly differed in count normalization, outlier exclusion, covariates, nominal versus adjusted p-values, enrichment gene lists and background. For example, the [JBX13 reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-1d54e4a7-8b0f-4224-bd31-efcfded0d46c.zip) removes three samples and models replicate, strain and medium; several answers retained all samples and omitted replicate. The [UBE2M reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-308d53bf-1513-4a09-913b-3a1112f94e7b.zip) removes KL3/WL3 before enrichment, unlike the `bix-53-q6` answer. Exact contributions were not isolated through reruns.
- `bix-10` / `bix-29` severity questions also expose a reference-definition caveat: the [reference preprocessing](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-fbe0e950-76f2-4eb7-a216-a2d377970922.zip), cell 17, aggregates all adverse events per participant, although questions call the endpoint COVID severity. COVID-specific/event-level alternatives therefore need protocol adjudication.

Grading and reference findings:

- `bix-19-q2` is a calculation-versus-submission example: the agent computed **Cohen's d = 0.216284**, independently matching [reference cell 30](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-8c64b1fa-fdcc-41e2-be8d-2f0c8d5faaa1.zip), but submitted approximately **0.22**. That final answer falls outside the target interval **0.215–0.217**. Other precision candidates include 35.34% versus 35% and 5.23 versus 5.2. The 11 cases are `4-q1/q5/q6`, `11-q1/q2/q5`, `19-q2`, `28-q6`, `38-q1/q3`, and `54-q5`, all with prefix `bix-`. Tiny nonzero p-values are not automatically equivalent to literal zero; `54-q5` also has a model-input difference alongside its ratio/fraction representation.
- `bix-53-q4` has a confirmed malformed target: the question requests a **pathway count**, but the [original ideal answer](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/BixBench.jsonl) is **4.25E-04**. [Reference cell 79](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-308d53bf-1513-4a09-913b-3a1112f94e7b.zip) explicitly counts **2** pathways. The submitted answer was **1**, so fixing the target would not automatically make it correct.
- `bix-31-q2` contradicts its stated analysis. The target interval **−0.45 to −0.35** conflicts with **abs(LFC)>0.5**. [Reference cells 32–38](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-b1dbace7-f6e9-42ec-81e1-bcc24161cc27.zip) show FAM138A at baseMean **0.483698**, unshrunk LFC **−0.383938**, and shrunk LFC **−0.060666**. The target matches the unshrunk, low-expression row despite instructions requiring shrinkage and baseMean>10. The agent answered `NA`.
- `bix-52-q1` has a reference-data bug: [reference cell 14](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-4dceea58-7d66-4576-bfc6-88c026d5b7a9.zip) downloads **JD_Chromosome_Length.csv** into **ZF_Chromosome_Length.csv**. The agent's **1.52** ratio is internally consistent with the supplied lengths and site counts; the provenance of the target **0.47–0.67** remains unresolved. `bix-52-q5` also counts repeated records instead of distinct sites, so this data caveat does not explain all CpG failures.
- The remaining four primary adjudication cases are `bix-8-q6` (260 unique genes versus 680 transcript records; [reference cell 21](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-48a6b469-9c9d-4bef-b5b4-f29b7d6fa046.zip) counts rows), `bix-38-q6` (median of paired ratios versus ratio of group medians), `bix-43-q4` (8/514 DE genes versus 8/49 pathway genes), and `bix-22-q6` (the origin of the 0.3–0.4 correlation target was not established). These require explicit definitions or reference reconstruction.
- `bix-54-q4` additionally has reversed target interval bounds, but its submitted p-value lies outside even the sorted interval. This metadata defect does not rescue that answer.

The [verifier](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/97037f793efaae22e22da5b89bc9604d2e40e800/adapters/bixbench/src/bixbench/task-template/tests/llm_judge.py) asks an LLM for binary equivalence. It has **no separate global numerical-tolerance rule**; some targets contain explicit intervals. The JSON-schema repair changes response format, not this comparison prompt. Before any rescoring, define a consistent precision/adjudication policy and preserve the present native grades as a separate baseline.

The 14 missing-answer traces show long model fits, repeated workbook inspection, unresolved analysis choices, and sensitivity checks after intermediate results existed. More time alone is not a demonstrated fix. The two exit-137 cases show killed statistical processes; excessive worker creation is a plausible contributor, but an OOM cause is unconfirmed. One gateway failure and `bix-10-q2`'s persistent judge 503 remain ungraded. The latter has a saved answer outside its target interval, but no manual grade was substituted.

Next: adjudicate the flagged question/reference and precision cases; document the intended analysis protocols; then select a small set of failures for any separately approved controlled rerun. Keep any revised scoring or solver results separate from this baseline. The existing verifier JSON-format PR follow-up remains open.

Reference links above use dataset revision `f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a`; notebook cell indices are zero-based. Several phylogenetic and genomic-pipeline capsules contain no reference notebook, which limits causal conclusions for the 14 unresolved cases.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 Agent-runtime summary for the [completed 205-question BixBench CLI run](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667). Measured from each original Harbor trial’s `agent_execution.started_at` and `finished_at`; all 205 have both timestamps.

The median agent runtime was **5.6 minutes per question**. The middle 50% took **1.7–15.5 minutes**, and the 90th percentile was **37.3 minutes**.

| Questions | n | Median, min | 25th–75th percentile, min | 90th percentile, min | Mean, min |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| All attempted questions | 205 | 5.6 | 1.7–15.5 | 37.3 | 12.8 |
| Solver completed without interruption | 185 | 4.7 | 1.6–13.8 | 20.5 | 8.6 |
| Final grade: correct | 101 | 2.3 | 0.9–9.2 | 17.3 | 6.9 |
| Final grade: incorrect | 86 | 8.1 | 2.8–14.8 | 26.5 | 12.3 |

These are elapsed solving times, including model responses, command execution, waits and tool/network latency during the agent phase. They exclude separately timed sandbox setup, agent setup and grading. Quantiles use linear interpolation at `(n−1)×p`.

**17/205 tasks (8.3%) reached the configured 3,600-second agent cap**: 14 had no submitted answer and remained ungraded; 3 retained gradeable answers. The other three interrupted agents had two process-kill failures and one gateway failure. Capped times measure time spent before termination, not the uncensored time required to solve those tasks. Recorded capped durations were 3,600.0–3,602.3 seconds.

The median complete trial duration, including setup, grading and teardown, was **7.3 minutes**. The interval from the first trial start to the last trial finish was **3 h 28 min 48 s**.

The 185 uninterrupted solver completions include one answer whose judge still failed. Correct/incorrect rows use final saved-answer recovery grades and retain the three scored timeouts. Runtime differences between outcome groups are descriptive; task difficulty and workflow differences confound interpretation.

The complete launcher-to-export span was **3 h 36 min 11 s**, with a cap of **16 concurrent trials**. That batch span includes setup and final export; later saved-answer judge recovery is excluded. The [existing result](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667) remains 101/187 correct with 18 ungraded.

Per-question times, raw timestamps, source hashes and the summary calculation are retained in the private evaluation handoff. No new evaluation or grading calls were made.
