| [bix-38-q1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-975f3e91-53b0-44b1-ac9f-20023d9c8cd0.zip) | 2.18-fold (fungi / animals) → 2x larger in fungi | **Presentation-equivalent candidate**. 2.18-fold agrees with the coarse 2x target. Recomputed ratio of full-precision group medians is 2.177433; ratio of rounded IQ-TREE report medians is 2.177509. | Accept only in a separately versioned policy allowing equivalence at the displayed reference precision; do not change the native grade. |
| [bix-38-q3](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-975f3e91-53b0-44b1-ac9f-20023d9c8cd0.zip) | 5.22% → 5% | **Presentation-equivalent candidate**. 5.22% rounds to 5%; saved calculation is 13/249 = 5.2209%. | Accept only in a separately versioned policy allowing equivalence at the displayed reference precision; do not change the native grade. |
| [bix-38-q6](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-975f3e91-53b0-44b1-ac9f-20023d9c8cd0.zip) | 1.9036 → 2.178 | **Confirmed task/reference defect**. Independent Newick branch-length sums find 96 paired orthologs and median(fungal_length/animal_length) = 1.9036165971, matching the submission. The target 2.178 instead matches the ratio of separately rounded group medians, 3.0962/1.4219 = 2.1775089669; that uses all 249 fungal and 100 animal trees. Full-precision group medians give 2.177433, also a different estimand. | Keep the paired-ratio question; reference 1.9036165971 with a declared tolerance, or explicitly request 1.904 to three decimal places. Preserve the paired ortholog list and full-precision input calculation. |
| [bix-43-q4](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-15ff11e5-2db1-45b6-b3a3-46bc2a74b821.zip) | 8/514 → 8/49 | **Unresolved analysis specification**. The prompt asks for the proportion of differentially expressed genes, but reference cell 65 reports the Enrichr overlap 8/49, whose denominator is pathway members. Agent 8/514 uses its DEG denominator. The notebook has 679 pre-mapping DEG rows at cell 45 and drops missing gene names at cell 53; the final distinct mapped denominator was not established. | Minimal repair: ask for the Enrichr Overlap field, explicitly defined as intersecting genes / pathway genes, and retain 8/49. If retaining the DEG-proportion wording, establish mapping/deduplication and recompute that denominator. Do not certify 514 as the reference count. |
| [bix-52-q1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-4dceea58-7d66-4576-bfc6-88c026d5b7a9.zip) | Chromosome W / chromosome 1 = 1.52 → Between 0.47 and 0.67 inclusive | **Confirmed task/reference defect**. Packaged ZF_Chromosome_Length.csv is byte-identical to JD_Chromosome_Length.csv (SHA256 59e321ef…051b); notebook cell 14 downloads the JD file under the ZF name. Three W and 29 chr1 distinct filtered sites give 1.519930 with that supplied table. The original Zenodo ZF table gives W length 20,846,394 and chr1 length 114,020,016, yielding 0.56581364, inside the existing 0.47–0.67 interval. | Replace the mislabeled capsule asset and notebook download URL with the original ZF table (Zenodo record 12205202, MD5 b078a4dab5b677bfd0742452de6b1a17). Retain the existing target interval. Future evaluation needs the corrected input; do not retroactively penalize the agent for using the supplied file. |
| [bix-53-q4](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-308d53bf-1513-4a09-913b-3a1112f94e7b.zip) | 1 → 4.25E-04 | **Confirmed task/reference defect**. The original dataset ideal is 4.25E-04 for a question asking how many pathways. Notebook cell 79 explicitly counts two oxidative terms among the top twenty. The submitted one is not correct merely because the gold is malformed. | Use integer target 2 only with the notebook's intended cohort, adjusted-p filtering, shrinkage and pathway-term matching explicitly specified. The current question says p while the notebook filters padj; pin that distinction before a corrected task is released. |
| [bix-54-q5](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-9e52daf6-ca58-43e8-e732-fbac3459d295.zip) | 10:1 → Between 0.9 and 0.99 inclusive | **Presentation-equivalent candidate**. 10:1 converts to a component fraction 10/11 = 0.90909, inside 0.90–0.99. Reference cells 16/19 use rhlI/(rhlI+lasI) and yield a spline maximum at 0.9076577. The prompt asks for a ratio but the target stores a fraction. The agent selected the best tested ratio from 36 mixed-culture rows; the reference spline used 39 rows, so final-answer equivalence does not validate the method. | State that the answer is the rhlI fraction; allow an explicitly labeled equivalent mixture ratio if retaining outcome-only grading. Keep the method caveat separate. |

Evidence uses the pinned BixBench dataset `f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a`; task links above point to the corresponding source capsule. Notebook cell numbers are zero-based. Local reproduction records include the downloaded-member SHA256 manifest, gene/correlation checks, and all 96 paired tree ratios. The corrected Zebra Finch file is available in [the original Zenodo dataset](https://zenodo.org/records/12205202).

A separate [public BixBench audit](https://github.com/Anqi-Dai/BixBench_eval/blob/6070dc293677b0ef21fa38d7ab23c5850d8799c0/env/REVIEW_REPORT.md) independently documents the 680-record/260-gene mismatch. Its study covers three capsules and fourteen questions; it does not validate this entire run.

The proposed precision rule was also screened against **all 205 saved outcomes, including the 101 previously correct answers**. This was a conservative scalar/range screen, not a complete semantic regrade: 81 answers require semantic parsing, and counts, unit conversions, reversed ranges and the zero p-value need explicit treatment. It flags two existing passes that a naive comparator would reject: `bix-18-q5` supplies 0.29 against a percent-scale 25–30 target, and `bix-45-q1` supplies 7.70e-54 against 7.6968e-54. The latter needs symmetric handling of reported precision, rather than always requiring the target's extra digits. These findings block adopting a blanket rounding rule or publishing a selectively corrected accuracy.

Harbor Index provides relevant prior work: its public index includes five BixBench-derived tasks, with eighteen trials each. [Its Jackdaw notes](https://hub.harborframework.com/tasks/harbor-index/bix-cpg-density-jackdaw/latest) explicitly say the scientific derivation was not re-audited. Later [PR #142](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-index/pull/142) fixed underspecified instructions for two tasks present in this run: miRNA analysis `bix-30-q1` ([issue #97](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-index/issues/97)) and ordinal regression `bix-10-q2` ([issue #113](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-index/issues/113)). The fixes specify preprocessing/modeling choices while retaining the targets. These are useful precedents for task repair, not grounds for changing our recorded grades. The index uses its own 1,200-second budgets and deterministic numeric verifiers; its results are not directly comparable to this baseline.

Next: review the seven local upstream-report drafts; agree on versioned task repairs and numerical tolerances; then validate any revised grader across all 205 outcomes before publishing a separate result. The fourteen other numerical/pipeline discrepancies and ungraded outcomes remain follow-ups. The main issue table records **per-question agent time**, with no total-duration column.

comments.body:
🤖 The pilot is idle with no GPU jobs running. Both planned 10-step attempts stopped in tiny-model preflight before student loading. Working Snowball SFT precedents now include a report on the same September 21 checkpoint, but the exact training path is not yet matched to this pilot. Resume after obtaining a reproducible working revision/configuration and reviewing the remaining differences. The baseline remains 0/1; the earlier four-step model’s incoherent evaluation remains ungraded.

<details>
<summary>Checkpoint, smoke findings, and next steps (September 23, 2026)</summary>

- **Hold further GPU runs; closer precedent identified (September 23):** The user supplied the text of [Harshit Varma’s report](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1374989195109466122/1552425627976474645). It continues the same `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21` checkpoint on filtered AgentTrove plus GLM-5.3 RST successes: 63,504 rows, two epochs/722 steps, batch 64, sequence 32,768, `5e-5` AdamH with cosine and 3% warmup. Reported held-out NLL improves 1.094 → 0.909 and parse-fail turns fall 67% → 25%, while premature completion, recovery, and long-context behavior regress. This supports a functioning SFT/serving path for our student, not a claim of improved overall TB2 performance. The screenshot does not give hardware, code revision, or the exact optimizer class.

  The completed four-step biology pilot used ordinary Adam at constant `5e-5`; the unexecuted ten-step plan uses ordinary Adam with cosine and no warmup. [Marin’s AdamH implementation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ca9511b8db88f120549f1c3c67eece49f5c52045/lib/levanter/src/levanter/optim/adamh.py) preserves matrix norms and uses separate parameter groups, so equal nominal learning rates do not imply equivalent updates. This is a material difference to review, not an established explanation for the earlier incoherent model or the preflight NaNs. The latter occurred before any optimizer update.

  [Luke’s pinned launch record](https://gist.github.com/lukedhlee/d152f86a58e8619a988361e1502f9e55) is a separate reproducible precedent: `lukedhlee/vista-snowball-sft@23d8fda7`, Grug trainer/AdamH, 16 × 4 GH200s, EP8, batch 64, sequence 32,768, and a different Stage-3 starting model. It cannot be substituted for Harshit’s unspecified setup without checking those differences. Further GPU submissions are on hold with the user’s agreement; preserve the 31 traces, baseline, and failed-run evidence. The resume condition is an exact successful training/export configuration, not a merge flag alone.

- **Working precedents and revised recommendation (September 23, 21:15 UTC):** [PR #9331](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9331) reports completed one-update Snowball SFT followed by FinanceBench evaluation: baseline 26/50, task-only 27/50, curriculum 23/50. Those results use an earlier unpacked, assistant-masked path; the PR explicitly distinguishes the later packed/full-text recipe, which has not been rerun on H100s. [Issue #9380](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9380) separately documents a 64-H100 run at step 135 with a usable HF export despite a final checkpoint rewrite error. Our two failed preflights establish a problem in the tested configuration, not a general Snowball SFT blocker. The next investigation should recover and compare a successful run’s exact revision, model, mesh, attention backend, and data path before proposing another allocation. #9328 [merged into the #9331 feature branch](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9328#issuecomment-5802057836), so its merged flag does not establish a new validated main-branch recipe. The Discord message was subsequently supplied as a screenshot; its report is summarized above. No additional GPU run was submitted.

- **Corrected GPU preflight failed (September 23, 19:28 UTC):** `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-cosine10-layoutfix-20260923-192616` passed the previous incompatible-sharding operation, then failed the strict native/previous gradient comparison with `AssertionError: (nan, nan)`. The recorded reference-gradient magnitude is NaN; the current logging does not identify the first affected parameter or establish whether the native gradient is also non-finite. CPU testing used reference attention; this GPU preflight uses `gpu_fa4_cute`, context parallelism, and a different tiny shape. The cause is unresolved, and this does not establish a failure of the 10-step schedule or the full student. **Zero student updates, no new trained checkpoint, all four GPU tasks terminal.** No tolerances were relaxed and no further GPU retry was submitted. Recommendation: resume after a maintainer-tested H100 forward/backward and usable HF-export path is available, then repeat preflight before training. Merge status alone does not establish those checks. Keep the 31 accepted traces, matched baseline, and agreed hyperparameters for that retry.

- **Corrected retry submitted (September 23, 19:26 UTC):** `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-cosine10-layoutfix-20260923-192616` uses pinned `ca9511b` plus the CPU-tested one-line layout correction described below. Output is `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=14d/bio-sft/bio-logistic-sft-sep21-cosine10-native-loss-layoutfix-20260923/`. The launcher verifies the original and patched source SHA256 before importing the model. Training remains ten cosine steps from `5e-5`, batch eight, length 4,096, fresh optimizer, and final BF16 export only, with zero automatic retries and a 75-minute cap. The matched original-task evaluation is prepared; 21 protocol fields and the task archive hash match the baseline. Evaluation waits for verified training/export completion.

- **CPU reproduction and candidate correction passed (September 23):** `/exedev/bio-native-loss-cpu-repro-20260923-191828` reproduced the exact native-loss `ShardingTypeError` using a tiny random Snowball model and 32 virtual CPU devices. Wrapping the per-token loss with `hax.auto_sharded(...)` before the existing weighted reduction resolved it. Against the preceding pilot loss, FP32 losses were **3.874972582 vs 3.874972820**, with maximum absolute gradient difference **2.24e-8**; BF16 loss and gradients matched exactly. Tolerances remain `atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-5`. This checks a targeted layout correction, not full-model GPU or generation correctness. The original GPU preflight remains required. A retry is prepared with the same 10 cosine steps, batch eight, sequence 4,096, original checkpoint, 32 H100s, and final export only. This adds one documented native-code correction to pinned `ca9511b`; The approved GPU retry is recorded above.

- **Native-loss preflight failed (September 23, 19:12 UTC):** `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-cosine10-20260923-191030` reached `loading_preflight → native_value_grad → Snowball.compute_next_token_loss → maybe_reduce_loss`, then raised `ShardingTypeError` at `arr * effective_weight`. The loss uses `((replica_dcn, data, expert), context)`; the mask uses `((replica_dcn, replica, data), None)`. Source: [Snowball loss at the tested revision](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ca9511b8db88f120549f1c3c67eece49f5c52045/lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/snowball.py#L838). This occurred on the tiny random model before student loading: **zero student updates and no new trained checkpoint**. All four GPU tasks are terminal. The 10-step cosine hypothesis remains untested. CPU-only job `/exedev/bio-native-loss-cpu-repro-20260923-191828` completed the failure reproduction and correction checks described above. It uses no pretrained weights and has a ten-minute cap. The approved GPU retry is recorded above.

- **Agreed experiment submitted (September 23, 19:10 UTC):** job `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-cosine10-20260923-191030` restarts from the original September 21 checkpoint with **10 updates, cosine decay from 5e-5, global batch eight, sequence 4,096, no packing**, and the native recipe's Adam settings. Eighty presentations are about 2.58 passes over 31 traces. The full conversations average 2,822 tokens and have a maximum of 3,477, so 4,096 preserves all examples. Use [PR #9328 at `ca9511b`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/ca9511b8db88f120549f1c3c67eece49f5c52045) for Snowball's native loss; the PR remains unmerged. The documented exceptions are the existing BF16 CPU import/native GPU placement helper and a thin Trainer driver with default checkpoint hooks disabled. This preserves the agreed final-BF16-export-only policy; the stock launcher would force a model-and-optimizer checkpoint. Distributed initialization precedes model config parsing; W&B and reference-code copying remain disabled. A tiny native/previous loss-and-gradient comparison, exact checkpoint round trip, and an 80-presentation corpus audit precede student loading. The same first training batch will be scored before and after each update; it remains training data and creates no validation split. Use 32 H100s with zero retries and the existing 75-minute cap. A newer maintainer-tested path can be tried when available.

- **Full regression audit completed (September 23):** CPU-only job `/exedev/bio-sft-weight-audit-20260923-183344` compared **67,078,882,816 values across 502 tensors and 39 shards**. Both checkpoints have zero non-finite values; no delta exceeds the conservative four-update Adam bound plus BF16 rounding. Global relative L2 change is **0.414%**. This reduces evidence for gross corruption but does not rule out harmful optimization or training semantics. Source/final tokenizer JSON, inference/training templates, and generation configuration match exactly. Full per-tensor report: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=14d/bio-sft/bio-sft-weight-audit-20260923-183344/report.json`.

- **Post-SFT evaluation stopped and preserved (September 23, 18:20 UTC):** `/exedev/snowball-sep21-bix51-post-sft-20260923-180511` produced incoherent, invalid JSON from its first response; later inspected responses remained incoherent. Harbor received SIGINT after approval and saved the trial as `CancelledError`: one attempted, zero graded, no answer, null reward, **496.04 seconds** of agent execution. This is not a scored benchmark failure. The parent is terminal and its eight-H100 inference child was released. A subsequent Daytona inventory found no owned sandbox. Canonical record: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/snowball-sep21-bix51-post-sft-20260923-180511/record.json`; sibling `results/protocol-stop.json` records the stop. Trajectory SHA256: `93b4bb468d4b09ad466903809711b01b0a6e1507009f51d5b42b770f99321c0f`.

- **Regression investigation:** sixteen evaluation settings and all task-file hashes match the coherent baseline. The tiny HF round-trip check and finite training losses do not establish full-model generation correctness after updates. The [native recipe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2163b2b4e50bdeb697f17433e296ad9fe842008f/experiments/sft/configs/snowball_h100.py) uses a base checkpoint, ten updates, and cosine decay from `5e-5`; this pilot continued an SFT checkpoint for four updates at constant `5e-5`. Those settings are not validated for this continuation. Too few updates may limit learning; an excessive learning rate, training error, or export/serving mismatch could explain the degradation. The completed weight audit and the subsequent cosine run are recorded above.

- **SFT and final export succeeded (September 23):** `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-native32h-20260923-174000` completed successfully on all four tasks. Its loader audit confirms **31 unique traces presented once**, four updates, one zero-loss padding slot, **26,963 supervised tokens**, and exclusion of the original task. Full-weight training used FP32 parameters/Adam, BF16 compute, batch eight, sequence 4,096, and learning rate 5e-5. Final export contains **39 shards and 502 tensors**, with **134,157,765,632 bytes of BF16 tensor data**; the complete index matches the source tensor names, total tensor bytes, and shard mapping. No optimizer or intermediate checkpoint was saved. Rank-zero timings: **154.36 seconds** to import/place/cast the student, **33.39 seconds** for the four updates, and **984.66 seconds (16.4 minutes)** for export. All updates had finite loss. This successful attempt used **11.45 recorded GPU-hours**; the eight native 32-GPU attempts total **43.30 GPU-hours**, excluding earlier eight-GPU experiments and the new evaluation. These are task-runtime figures, not a provider bill.

- **Trained artifact and evaluation:** `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=14d/bio-sft/bio-logistic-sft-sep21-1epoch-32h100-fixedio-20260923/hf/`; sibling `training-complete.json` records the audit, losses, timings, tensor count, and index SHA256. The matched evaluation `/exedev/snowball-sep21-bix51-post-sft-20260923-180511` was submitted at 18:05 UTC for **one attempt on unchanged `bix-51-q2`**, using eight H100s and the baseline's `/nothink` protocol. It checks the saved training-completion record, index, shard presence, and inference template before serving. Sixteen protocol fields and all task-file hashes match the baseline. The result is pending; this one-task test will not establish a benchmark-wide score or pass-rate estimate.

- **Preceding attempt stopped before student loading (September 23):** `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-native32g-20260923-171659` passed the tiny GPU-cast/import/export check: one finite optimizer update and all 103 BF16 HF tensors exactly preserved. The new I/O probe then failed because `get_fs_token_paths(..., mode="wb")` expands a scalar destination into `io-probe.safetensors/0.part`, while verification and cleanup targeted the parent as a file. This is a bug in the pilot probe. The corrected call uses `expand=False` and asserts the exact destination; a local file write/read/delete regression passed. No real student weights loaded in that failed attempt; the corrected retry is recorded above. All four tasks ended at 17:21:16 UTC, using **2.15 recorded GPU-hours**; the seven native 32-GPU attempts total **31.85 GPU-hours**, excluding earlier eight-GPU experiments. The corrected retry subsequently removed the probe's temporary `0.part` object. Provenance: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=14d/bio-sft/bio-logistic-sft-sep21-1epoch-32h100-gpucast-20260923/provenance/`.

- **Upstream SFT findings checked (September 23):** [PR #9316](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9316) is already the pilot's source revision. The newly reported failures have concrete scope: [#9372](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9372) initializes JAX during HF config parsing; the pilot initializes distributed JAX first. [#9373](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9373) concerns CUDA/NCCL setup; the pilot's distributed optimizer and compilation checks passed. [#9375](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9375) concerns W&B startup; the pilot disables W&B. [#9377](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9377) fails while copying reference code from S3; the pilot already uses `save_reference_code=False` and validates final metadata. [#9380](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9380) rewrites a saved final TensorStore checkpoint on resume; the pilot saves no TensorStore checkpoints and does not resume one. The reported 64-H100 run completed its HF export, although Iris marked that resume failed during final checkpoint writing. This does not establish a 64-GPU requirement for the shorter pilot, which already completed four updates on 32 H100s at sequence length 4,096.

- **CPU I/O measurement:** the prior CPU-only regional benchmark uploaded an existing 3,431,580,288-byte shard in **13.70 seconds with the native uploader**, versus **27.14 seconds with fsutil streaming**. Both full readbacks matched the source MD5, and both temporary copies were removed. Keep the native exporter. This does not explain the earlier slower H100-worker export. The current recovery retains the 45-second training-node upload gate and 75-minute cap; the corrected run completed full-model import and final export, with timings recorded above.

- **Training ran; export timed out (September 23):** the September 21 student completed all four planned full-weight SFT updates on **32 H100s**, using the 31 accepted traces once, FP32 parameters/Adam, BF16 compute, and no intermediate checkpoints. All four ranks logged update 4 with finite loss **1.2927228**. The first update took **303.7 seconds including compilation**; later retained update timings were **1.5–1.8 seconds**. These are different batches, so the losses do not establish improvement. The job then exceeded its 45-minute task cap during the final 39-shard HF export. At the last object inventory, five completed shards were present; the export is incomplete and unusable, and **post-SFT evaluation has not run**. All four GPU tasks are terminal. Recorded runtime was **24.27 GPU-hours** for this attempt and **29.70 GPU-hours across today's six native 32-GPU attempts**; this excludes earlier eight-GPU experiments and is task-runtime accounting, not a provider bill.

- **Remaining blocker:** checkpoint I/O dominates this short pilot. A stack captured the import callback converting BF16 to FP32 on the CPU; export logs show slow sequential shard uploads. A later CPU profile did not establish a single upload bottleneck. The preceding retry stopped in the probe path bug above. The corrected run subsequently completed import, training, and final export as recorded above. Resolve and measure the I/O path before another full attempt, then run the already prepared matched `/nothink` evaluation on unchanged `bix-51-q2`. The partial output stays under the existing `ttl=14d` prefix and must not be treated as a completed checkpoint.

- **Distributed preflight passed (September 23):** on four nodes / 32 H100s, a tiny Snowball completed one optimizer update with finite loss **5.5434394**. All **103 HF tensors matched exactly after BF16 export and reload** through the shared regional path. The 13.7 MB validation checkpoint was removed after the comparison. The real September 21 checkpoint subsequently loaded and completed four SFT updates; its final export timed out as recorded above. The launcher pins Python 3.12, includes Iris's CUDA 13 setup, and uses the shared path required by the rank-zero-only exporter. No numerical tolerance was relaxed. Source remains `2163b2b4e50bdeb697f17433e296ad9fe842008f`; task scripts and plan are saved under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=14d/bio-sft/bio-logistic-sft-sep21-1epoch-32h100-20260923/provenance/`.

- Compatibility checks before SFT: the cached tokenizer JSON differs from September 21 in its added-token table. A CPU audit verified **identical input IDs and assistant masks on all 31 traces**, so the existing cache is retained. Training and final export now load the September 21 tokenizer explicitly. The mesh is eight expert shards within each node and four context shards across nodes. Two preceding attempts stopped before reading student weights (mesh validation, then the tokenizer-file equality guard); all their GPU tasks are terminal, with **1.27 recorded GPU-hours** in total. The current job rechecks the cache against the selected tokenizer before loading weights. No post-SFT task grade is available yet.

- Hardware decision (September 23): target **32 H100s (four nodes)** with the [native Snowball recipe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2163b2b4e50bdeb697f17433e296ad9fe842008f/experiments/sft/configs/snowball_h100.py), FP32 parameters/Adam state, BF16 compute, and context=4/expert=8. Eight GPUs were a footprint preference, not a limit. The native eight-H100 probe failed its first optimizer update: it requested another 37.77 GiB/GPU with only 24.24 GiB available, after initializing about 51 GiB/GPU of BF16 training state. No student weights were loaded by that probe. Current attempt: `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-native32f-20260923-155632`. The 32-H100 job passed tiny distributed training/import/export and completed **one epoch, four updates** using the existing regional September 21 checkpoint. Its attempted final BF16 HF export was incomplete (~134 GB; no saved optimizer state). It has a 45-minute task cap and zero automatic retries. The upstream 64-H100 export report is recorded above; this pilot now has a complete trained export; the post-SFT grade remains pending.

- Updated backend investigation (September 23): [PR #9316](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9316) has merged a [native Levanter Snowball SFT path](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2163b2b4e50bdeb697f17433e296ad9fe842008f/experiments/sft/configs/snowball_h100.py). It supports direct HF loading and a final HF export without an intermediate Grug checkpoint. The one-epoch loader audit passed: 31 distinct traces, each once, four batches, one zero-loss padding slot, and 26,963 supervised tokens. That initial eight-H100 investigation is superseded by the 32-H100 attempt above.

- Numerical checks at `2163b2b4e50bdeb697f17433e296ad9fe842008f`: all imported/round-tripped weight tensors were exact. comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 GLM-5.3 completed the September 25 BixBench-Verified-50 run using merged Harbor main and Pi: **39 correct, 7 incorrect, 4 ungraded**. Accuracy among graded tasks is **84.78% (39/46)**; coverage is **92% (46/50)**. The four ungraded outcomes cannot all be attributed to the model. [EvalDash run](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/glm53-bixbench-verified50-pi-main-20260925-150940).

The run used [Marin a795b1d](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/a795b1d4306c71b1f4fc52cdcac2b5b1f0ed70d4), [Harbor 21e0ea6](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/tree/21e0ea6a0cc1a0b617aebd86988ea93e1795f84a), and [task snapshot 674c37c](https://github.com/gonzalobenegas/harbor-datasets/tree/674c37ca8b2e537d36a1886f6cba99f2c6bdaa2f/datasets/bixbench-verified-50). There was one fresh attempt per question, up to 16 concurrent trials, Pi 0.87.0, 32,768 tokens of total context, an 8,192-token per-response limit, an 8,192-token compaction reserve, and setup/agent/verifier limits of 360/1,800/300 seconds. Daytona storage was explicitly set to 10 GiB. Grading used decimal-precision-v1 and Together GPT-OSS-120B. Exact served weights revision was unavailable.

Pi was configured with `thinking=medium` and `thinking_format=chat-template`. The [provider registration](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/21e0ea6a0cc1a0b617aebd86988ea93e1795f84a/src/harbor/agents/installed/pi.py) disables `supportsReasoningEffort` and sends `enable_thinking`; “medium” therefore does not establish a provider-enforced medium reasoning budget. This applies the Pi runtime/budget settings from [#9409](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9409) to Verified-50; it is a different benchmark from that policy's 205-task BixBench CLI corrections set. The earlier Terminus-2 result also used different agent and time budgets, so the aggregate difference is not a controlled model comparison.

| Tasks | Saved evidence | Attribution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bix-30-q3`, `bix-53-q2` | Pi ended with `stopReason: length` after approximately 5m10s and 6m18s. The verifier explicitly reported that `/workspace/answer.txt` was absent. | Incomplete agent output under the response budget, combined with Pi/Harbor termination handling. No evidence of a judge service failure. |
| `bix-31-q2`, `bix-49-q4` | Both agents reached 30 minutes while a tool was still running; the last commands ran `notebook.py` and `deseq2_analysis.R`, respectively. Both subsequent verifiers timed out at 300 seconds. No answer or verifier-output artifact was recovered. | Agent time-budget exhaustion followed by verifier failures. Saved evidence does not establish why the computations took so long or where verification stalled. |

Source inspection and an offline replay on October 9 narrowed the harness behavior:

- [Pi 0.87.0's loop](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/16787ad5b2dc748047f314ca1bfe7708f30f54f3/packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts#L244-L319) can end after a length-limited response with no tool calls and no continuation. Harbor's pinned Pi validator only rejects a final `error`. Feeding that exact validator a synthetic `length` event returned exit 0; an `error` control returned exit 1. Thus a truncated response can reach verification as a normal agent exit. This reproduces the validator behavior, not the biological computation or model generation.
- [Daytona cancellation cleanup](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/21e0ea6a0cc1a0b617aebd86988ea93e1795f84a/src/harbor/environments/daytona/environment.py#L1860-L1907) cancels local polling and runs `pkill -9 -f opencode`. Pi does not pass a remote execution timeout in its run command. That leaves a concrete gap in stopping Pi and its children before shared-sandbox verification. Continued processes could interfere with verification; this is a plausible contributor, not a demonstrated cause of these two verifier timeouts. Missing verifier logs alone do not prove the grader never started, because Harbor downloads those logs after the exec completes.
- [Trial exception recording](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/21e0ea6a0cc1a0b617aebd86988ea93e1795f84a/src/harbor/trial/trial.py#L430-L452) deliberately lets the later exception replace the earlier one. A final `VerifierTimeoutError` therefore does not exclude an earlier agent timeout.
- The [Verified-50 grader](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/21e0ea6a0cc1a0b617aebd86988ea93e1795f84a/adapters/bixbench-verified-50/src/bixbench_verified50/template/tests/llm_judge.py#L76-L85) deliberately returns without reward when no answer exists. This is the pinned missing-submission convention, not a newly established grading bug. #9409 also does not automatically assign zero to Harbor agent errors. No grades were changed.

The saved launch configuration allowed up to 10 retries for an explicit infrastructure-exception list, but omitted `VerifierTimeoutError` and `RewardFileNotFoundError`. Consequently those failures were not automatically retried, despite #9409 classifying verifier timeouts as retryable infrastructure errors. This is a launch-policy mismatch for the two verifier timeouts.

The September 25 artifact inspection and sandbox inventory found no recoverable answer/workspace for verifier-only replay. No solver or judge calls were made during this diagnosis, and no verifier retry could be executed faithfully. On October 9 the old diagnostic job was no longer available through Iris and this VM lacked direct CoreWeave storage credentials; the new findings above come from the pinned source and offline validator replay, combined with the previously recorded artifact inspection.

Next: validate generic Pi process-tree cancellation and verifier isolation with a bounded harness reproduction, record response truncation explicitly, and decide the intended continuation behavior within the existing budget. Retain verifier logs and answer artifacts even on failure. Those checks should precede any fresh four-task solver retry. The biological causes of the long computations remain unresolved; [harbor#192](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/192) already tracks Verified-50 source/runtime concerns, including a separate earlier R failure.

🤖 Snowball v0.1 was unreliable at completing the agent workflow in this BiomniBench-DA configuration: **38 of 50 tasks ended without a nonempty report at either required path**. The mean benchmark score was **4.24/100**. This result combines submission failures with low rubric scores on the submitted work; it does not isolate biology knowledge from agent execution or model–harness integration. The trace audit found no evidence of a general report-collection defect, but does not establish that the serving and agent configuration was appropriate for this checkpoint.

[EvalDash run](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20261020-144256-open-athena-Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14-biomnibench-da-pi-volume-free50-e8bf). The displayed metric averages rubric points and missing-submission zeros; it is not accuracy. This run uses five input variants and substitutes MiniMax for the dataset's original judge. The adapter scorer also applies signed rubric penalties and validates complete criterion coverage; the released scorer parses unsigned points. Comparisons with published results require matching these choices. No reference model was evaluated under this same protocol. This is supplementary to the Snowball v0.1 release evaluations in [#10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197); their benchmark set and aggregate are unchanged.

| Final submission state | Tasks |
| --- | ---: |
| Both nonempty reports preserved and rubric-graded | 5 |
| One nonempty report preserved and rubric-graded | 7 |
| Neither report nonempty at the required paths; native zero | 38 |
| Total | 50 |

A missing submission means neither `/app/trace.md` nor `/app/answer.txt` contained text beyond whitespace at verification time. It does not establish that the model did no analysis or lacked a biological answer: some traces contain attempted analyses, simulated execution, or reports written elsewhere.

The score decomposes into **24% submission coverage × 17.67/100 mean score among the 12 submitted tasks = 4.24/100 overall** (conditional mean rounded). Only five tasks supplied both reports. The 12-task mean describes a selected subset under this judge and scorer; it does not estimate how the other 38 would score after fixing submission. Submission failures account for 38 zeros, while the submitted work also received low rubric scores.

Structured events from the selected final-attempt Pi logs for all 50 logical tasks were audited, with detailed inspection of the examples below. The table assigns each missing-submission task once: the four specific submission failures take precedence; the remaining 34 are grouped by termination. Filename checks use executed tool arguments and do not by themselves prove that no indirect write was attempted.

| Observed termination or submission failure | Tasks |
| --- | ---: |
| Normal model stop; no executed tool argument contained `trace.md` or `answer.txt` | 22 |
| Per-response output limit reached before submission | 11 |
| Agent timeout at 30 minutes | 1 |
| Both reports written under `/app/analysis/` instead of `/app/` | 1 |
| Empty `answer.txt` and no `trace.md` | 1 |
| Malformed write arguments rejected by the tool | 1 |
| Analysis script failed before writing reports | 1 |
| Total | 38 |

These are observations from the saved events, not 38 independently established checkpoint defects. Ten of the 11 output-limit cases generated thousands of repetitions of “Now.” All 11 consumed the configured 16,384 output tokens. Pi then ended without another solver turn; this termination behavior contributes to missing submissions under the evaluated protocol. The [earlier Verified-50 investigation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6086246928) documents the same Pi behavior with length-limited responses.

Examples distinguish execution from text that only describes execution. The links open in Hugging Face’s Agent Trace Viewer:

- [`da-26-2`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/biomni-da-26-2.jsonl) executed zero tools but generated terminal-control JSON followed by a simulated `<user> New Terminal Output` block, including directory listings and missing-package errors. Those observations are assistant-generated text, as in BixBench [`bix-28-q6`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bix-28-q6.jsonl); they do not establish that the commands ran. This BiomniBench example does not simulate a successful report submission.
- [`da-10-1`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/biomni-da-10-1.jsonl) received successful write confirmations for `/app/analysis/trace.md` and `/app/analysis/answer.txt`. The prompt and verifier require `/app/trace.md` and `/app/answer.txt`. Its 20 tool dispatches include those real writes; the final assistant response also contains a simulated terminal verification transcript, which is not another execution. Missing submission here does not mean no report was produced.
- [`da-17-5`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/biomni-da-17-5.jsonl) streamed malformed JSON for a report write. Replaying the saved argument deltas through Pi 0.87.0 and its exact `partial-json` 0.1.7 dependency reproduced the parsed `{ "path": "/app/trace.md" }` argument and missing-content validation failure. A valid multiline-JSON control parsed correctly. After the rejected write, the model left a report in chat and stopped. This resembles BFCL’s chat-only submission behavior, illustrated by [`bfcl-multiple-170`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bfcl-multiple-170.jsonl) and [`bfcl-parallel-147`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bfcl-parallel-147.jsonl), while adding a distinct write-argument failure.
- [`da-18-1`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/biomni-da-18-1.jsonl) executed 10 tool calls, then generated a response containing 8,041 occurrences of “Now” and ended with `length` at 16,384 output tokens, without the reports. This closely resembles BixBench [`bix-13-q2`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bix-13-q2.jsonl). These token and repetition counts describe the final response, not the full trajectory.

The [HF collection](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples) includes original event logs and selected verifier verdict fields for all four examples. Viewer copies minimally adapt completed Pi messages while preserving their content; compaction events are labeled import annotations. Private judge connection settings are omitted from the verifier copies. Uploaded originals and adapted files were verified against local hashes, and all four viewers preserve the recorded tool-call counts.

Together with the [BixBench/BFCL audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6300963037), these examples show recurring execution and submission failures across benchmarks: simulated environment observations, answers left in chat, and repetitive output-limit termination. BiomniBench also demonstrates wrong-directory report writes and malformed write arguments. This strengthens the evidence that the submission problem extends beyond biological reasoning, but the four purposively selected traces do not estimate each mechanism’s prevalence or establish a common cause. BixBench used Pi 1.3.0; BFCL and this BiomniBench run used Pi 0.87.0. No biological calculations were independently recomputed or regraded in this comparison.

All 50 initial prompts contained the required absolute output paths. Reports from 12 tasks were preserved and rubric-graded; three successful direct writes were also compared byte-for-byte with their archived verifier files and matched. Native per-task rewards, the sealed 50-row sample archive, and the canonical/EvalDash mean agree. Missing submissions receive zero before any judge call, so those 38 zeros do not depend on MiniMax's rubric judgments. No scores were repaired and no new model calls were made during the audit.

An independent review recomputed the 212 total points, mean, coverage, and failure counts from the saved task records. The audit bundle referenced below contains the per-task summaries, inspected trace details, parser replay, and audit scripts.

The evidence implicates several stages of execution. Repetition is an observed generation failure; Pi ending after a length-limited response is a harness behavior that can prevent a later submission. Invalid tool formats could reflect checkpoint behavior or a serving/interface mismatch. Successful report collection on other tasks argues against a general collection defect, but does not resolve those integration questions. The audit cannot attribute all 38 failures to the checkpoint or determine whether the weakness is biology-specific.

The next useful comparisons would be a reference model on the identical protocol and a small controlled Snowball diagnostic capturing raw model tokens, API requests/responses, and executed tools. The former would test whether this setup permits another model to complete the tasks; the latter would help separate checkpoint, template/parser, sampling, and serving effects. Pi events retain API text and argument deltas, but the inspected artifacts do not contain pre-parser model token captures. Neither comparison has been run; no diagnostic GPU rerun has been launched.

<details>
<summary>Protocol and reproducibility</summary>

- Model: [open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14/tree/6783e9743478bd25a9ce03ab3460e84d6a9814b0), revision `6783e9743478bd25a9ce03ab3460e84d6a9814b0` (v0.1).
- Dataset: [phylobio/BiomniBench-DA](https://huggingface.co/datasets/phylobio/BiomniBench-DA/tree/e1c8ca5e11a620087bc48d97888eb69176a1f235), revision `e1c8ca5e11a620087bc48d97888eb69176a1f235`; all 50 public tasks, no held-out tasks. The `derived-input-v1` variant uses 45 native-input tasks and five existing input variants: `da-1-3`/`da-1-4` omit an unused counts matrix; `da-17-1`/`da-17-3`/`da-17-5` use the previously pinned all-cell raw-count H5AD, omitting normalized expression and embeddings. Questions, required outputs, and rubrics are unchanged.
- Runtime: [Marin 75a5690](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/75a5690b0ff2e1510d73e576649e3e059f06da9a), [Harbor 016dd78](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/tree/016dd78b301b621ee4089f2da5776ebe80236820), Pi 0.87.0. BixBench execution settings from [policy #10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197): 65,536 total-context tokens, 16,384 output tokens per response, 32,768 compaction reserve; 360/1,800/300-second setup/agent/verifier limits; 16 concurrent trials. Daytona used at most 8 GiB RAM and 10 GiB disk, with no volumes.
- Serving: Snowball on 8 H100s, TP=1/DP=8 with expert parallelism and the native chat template; Hermes tool parser, no reasoning parser, `thinking_format=chat-template`. Judge served by a separate eight-H100 Iris job: [MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8/tree/c5454eb03678d8710e54a4e0fc681b9f3b4a3dba), revision `c5454eb03678d8710e54a4e0fc681b9f3b4a3dba`, TP=8; temperature 0, 8,192 output tokens, native rubric levels, scores divided by 100 for Marin's reward metric. This replaces the dataset's original judge configuration.
- There were 50 logical trials and 52 physical solver attempts. Two verifier timeouts triggered the policy's automatic infrastructure retries; both failed attempts and their replacements retain separately readable result records and Pi logs. The separate preliminary pilot is excluded. The evaluator succeeded, both serving jobs terminated, and the final Daytona inventory found no sandboxes belonging to this run or its preflight.
- Source/configuration archive: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/20261020-144256-open-athena-Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14-biomnibench-da-pi-volume-free50-e8bf/provenance/source-and-input-manifest.tar.gz`, SHA-256 `9e879d9db20d7f4ca0e7e5e12737ae0340b66b0a547e1b6c89dea1d76c4c84ad`. It contains `launch_full.py`, the task/input manifest, and exact configurations. The campaign was placed under `experiments/evaluation/campaigns/biomnibench-da-volume-free50-20261020/` in the pinned Marin workspace. Execution used the canonical `prepare_evaluation_batch` and `run_evaluation_batch` functions in the same CPU orchestrator after remote staging and sandbox preflight. The submitted entry point was:

  python -c 'import runpy; runpy.run_path("experiments/evaluation/campaigns/biomnibench-da-volume-free50-20261020/launch_full.py", run_name="__main__")'

Upload and readback hashes match. comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 Snowball v0.1’s official BixBench result is **19/205 = 9.27%**, reported as **9.3%** in the [release results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10283). A saved-trace audit shows that missing submissions account for most failed tasks.

| Final outcome | Tasks |
| --- | ---: |
| Missing `/workspace/answer.txt`; automatic zero | 156 |
| Empty answer sent to judge; rejected | 1 |
| Nonempty answer rejected by judge | 29 |
| Answer accepted by judge | 19 |
| **Total** | **205** |

All 205 tasks received scores, but only **48 contained nonempty submitted answers**. Full scoring coverage should therefore not be interpreted as full submission coverage.

Among the 156 missing-file cases, **141 had a final assistant event with `stopReason=stop`** and **15 had `stopReason=length`**. Here, `stop` is Pi’s normal-end status for the model response, distinct from `length`; it does not establish that the agent completed the task or wrote the required file. Pi 1.3.0 also maps a null provider finish reason to `stop`, so the status alone does not prove an intentional completion decision. Across the run, 22 selected traces contained no tool-execution-start events; inspected examples generated tool-call markup or simulated terminal output as ordinary assistant text (for example, [`bix-28-q6`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bix-28-q6.jsonl)). All initial prompts specified the required answer path. These observations overlap: the 22 tasks are not an additional failure category.

The [public trace examples](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples) open in Hugging Face’s Agent Trace Viewer. Seven BixBench examples and four BFCL follow-up examples include their original logs and verifier output. Because this Harbor run used Pi with `--no-session`, the viewer copies minimally adapt completed event messages into Pi session entries; message content is unchanged, and compaction events are labeled import annotations.

The traces show several distinct problems:

- **Missing submissions (three examples):** [`bix-10-q1`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bix-10-q1.jsonl) performed an analysis and stated an odds ratio in chat, but never created the required answer file. The [verifier log](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/verifier/bix-10-q1.txt) records the missing file. Its computed odds ratio, approximately **1.169**, also falls outside the [pinned reference range of 1.50–1.54](https://github.com/penfever/harbor-datasets/blob/454d04b5427fd90de78d7bec9dfe57561a21ff03/datasets/bixbench-cli-marin-corrections-1/bix-10-q1/tests/ground_truth.json). Writing that value would have fixed submission completeness, but not the reference mismatch; the underlying analysis has not been independently recomputed. Two further missing-file examples illustrate different behaviors: [`bix-28-q6`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bix-28-q6.jsonl) ended with `stop` after generating an entire simulated execution transcript inside one assistant text response, with zero executed tool calls. It supplied its own shell observations and numerical result, then showed code supposedly writing `0.1258380127877238` to `/workspace/answer.txt` and a simulated `cat` confirming it. None of those operations ran: this was simulated execution and submission, not merely omission of the save instruction, and the numerical result has no verified execution behind it; [`bix-13-q2`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bix-13-q2.jsonl) executed 18 tool calls but ended in repetitive generation with `length`, also without an answer file. Their verifier logs confirm the missing files ([bix-28-q6](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/verifier/bix-28-q6.txt), [bix-13-q2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/verifier/bix-13-q2.txt)).
- **Repetition and length limits:** 11 of the 15 length-stop cases contained over 1,000 occurrences of “Now” in one response (for example, [`bix-13-q2`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bix-13-q2.jsonl)). Fourteen ended with a response reporting 16,384 output tokens. In the remaining case, [`bix-30-q5`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bix-30-q5.jsonl), the final response reported 65,535 input tokens and one output token; its trace also records failed compaction and failed context-overflow recovery. These counts describe the final response, not the entire task trajectory.
- **Analysis errors:** [`bix-35-q3`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bix-35-q3.jsonl) used the BUSCO `Score` column as an evolutionary rate despite the question specifying PhyKIT `evo_rate`. [`bix-27-q2`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bix-27-q2.jsonl) reported 7,992 accumulated classifications across 50 iterations for a question asking how many samples were consistently classified.
- **Grading concern:** [`bix-8-q5`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bix-8-q5.jsonl) submitted `8.10e-194` and received zero against a reference of `p < 2.2e-16`. The [verifier log](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/verifier/bix-8-q5.txt) preserves the submitted answer, reference, and rejection. The submitted value satisfies that inequality. This merits adjudication, although the underlying analysis has not been independently recomputed.

Compaction errors appeared in **29 tasks**, including some that eventually submitted answers; these observations overlap with the categories above. Across all 205 final trials, compaction count showed little association with a missing answer file (Pearson r = 0.052; Spearman ρ = −0.005). Missing-file rates were **94/122 (77.0%) without compaction** and **62/83 (74.7%) with at least one compaction event** (two-sided Fisher p = 0.74). Tasks with a compaction error had 24/29 missing files, versus 132/176 without an error (82.8% versus 75.0%; Fisher p = 0.48). Counts include successful and failed compaction-end events; using only successful events also gave little association (Pearson r = 0.035). These are unadjusted observational comparisons: task difficulty and trajectory length may affect both compaction and outcomes, so they neither establish causation nor rule out harm in individual traces.

This audit examined structured events from all 205 selected final trajectories, with detailed inspection of the examples above. The run had 211 physical attempts: six verifier-timeout attempts preceded replacements. The final per-task rewards match the sealed sample archive. An independent review reproduced the outcome and event counts from the saved records and traces, and verified all 205 unique task IDs, logical trial IDs, and rewards against the sealed sample shard. Neither audit independently recomputed the biological analyses. No grades changed and no solver or judge calls were made.

Missing submissions also occurred in the same checkpoint’s **BFCL parity evaluation**: **55/123 final trials (44.7%)** explicitly failed because `/app/result.json` was absent. This BFCL evaluation required a JSON description of the selected benchmark function call(s) in `/app/result.json`, written using Pi’s actual tools. The remaining outcomes were 42 accepted submissions, 25 rejected submissions, and one JSON parsing error; the parsing error is not counted as a confirmed empty answer. These counts come from the [saved BFCL result records](s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/20261019-104642-open-athena-Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14-bfclparity-pi-e8cb/results/) identified in the [release archive map](https://gist.github.com/penfever/b7deea3a2eaec1642a56c0d67ba1e41a#file-trace_archive_source_prefixes-json). BFCL used **Pi 0.87.0**, versus **Pi 1.3.0** here. A follow-up inspected four missing-file traces: the lexicographically first missing trial in each of the irrelevance, multiple, parallel, and simple-python categories. This selection illustrates mechanisms; it does not estimate their prevalence among the 55 missing submissions.

All four inspected BFCL traces ended with `stop`, had no compaction events, and failed the file-existence check despite an explicit instruction to execute a write to `/app/result.json`:

- [`bfcl-multiple-170`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bfcl-multiple-170.jsonl) selected `soccer_stat.get_player_stats` for Ronaldo’s 2019–2020 season and emitted the proposed JSON in chat, with zero tool executions. The content follows the requested player and season, but was not submitted or regraded.
- [`bfcl-parallel-147`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bfcl-parallel-147.jsonl) described three `light_travel_time` calls and considered both `echo` and heredoc commands for writing the file, but executed neither. It ended with JSON in chat and zero tool executions. Recognizing the write requirement did not translate into executing it.
- [`bfcl-irrelevance-103`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bfcl-irrelevance-103.jsonl) made six real tool calls to inspect the environment, then said it would write the result but only emitted JSON in chat. It also selected `weather_forecast.get` for a current-time question; the described weather function does not meet that request, so the prompt’s no-applicable-function branch calls for `[]`. This is a function-selection mistake in addition to a submission failure.
- [`bfcl-simple-python-161`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bfcl-simple-python-161.jsonl) attempted to invoke `crime_statute_lookup` as a live agent tool and received `Tool crime_statute_lookup not found`. The task required writing a JSON description of the call. After six actual shell calls, it stopped without writing the file; its final text contained a `<tool_response>` imitation of the earlier Python-version output, not another tool execution. The seven execution-start events include the rejected unknown-tool dispatch.

These examples extend the evidence for general instruction-following and tool-use problems beyond biology: leaving answers in chat, describing writes without executing them, and confusing benchmark function descriptions with live agent tools. None of these four reproduces the complete fabricated execution and successful-file-write transcript in `bix-28-q6`. The final tool-response imitation in `bfcl-simple-python-161` is a narrower resemblance. Different Pi versions and the small purposive sample prevent attributing all missing submissions to one mechanism. Original logs and verifier outputs accompany each linked HF trace; no BFCL answers were regraded.

The terminal suites provide additional examples: OpenThoughts-TBLite reported missing `answer.txt` in five trials across two tasks, and Terminal-Bench reported missing `result.txt` in three trials across two tasks. These are confirmed subsets, not overall failure rates; both suites used Terminus-2 and repeated each task three times. Conversely, all 200 DS-1000 trials had nonempty saved code submissions. Missing files, wrong submitted answers, and agent timeouts should therefore remain separate outcomes when comparing these evaluations.

The evaluated configuration used **Smartie Step14, `bixbench-cli-marin-corrections@3`, Pi 1.3.0, and MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 judging**. A substantial part of the observed failure burden concerns general tool execution and answer submission, limiting what the overall score tells us about biological reasoning. In particular, the simulated execution in [`bix-28-q6`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples/blob/main/sessions/bix-28-q6.jsonl) provides evidence of a tool-use failure, not an executed biological analysis whose correctness can be assessed. The BFCL trace inspection demonstrates related submission and tool-use failures beyond biology, while leaving the frequency and shared cause of each mechanism unresolved. Question-specific concerns also remain: the wrong evolutionary-rate column and classification-count interpretation are analysis errors, and the odds-ratio result disagrees with the pinned reference. Writing the missing answer file would not resolve that disagreement; the underlying analysis has not been independently recomputed. The evidence does not isolate checkpoint behavior from serving, tool parsing, or harness behavior; a controlled diagnostic should test those boundaries before interpreting this score as a measure of biological reasoning alone.

- Model: `open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14`, revision `6783e9743478bd25a9ce03ab3460e84d6a9814b0`.
- Run: `20261019-104831-open-athena-Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14-bixbench-pi-72d5`.
- Marin revision: `36008e797f7e7cc65a00e70afd962eea0e8d54ca`; Harbor revision: `38742b0f9f411c95e0c01468785cac7bb77c9894`.

- Judge: `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8`, revision `c5454eb03678d8710e54a4e0fc681b9f3b4a3dba`.

- Sealed sample manifest: `ccc282fcfada4e2a8e493d9a7a001cbc`; sample-shard SHA-256: `0de718285342fe38cd1cb5776769a537bc9f3ae3ab960326f330f14db6cb8ffa`. All 205 sample rewards agree with the native final records.

</details>

🤖 GLM-5.3 completes the BiomniBench-DA reporting workflow much more often than Snowball v0.1 under the same task and agent policy. The first-attempt comparison already establishes this difference without crediting infrastructure retries. The shared harness also exhibits verifier failures, so this experiment does not establish that every Snowball failure originates in the checkpoint.

The reference run ended with an infrastructure failure after the judge and then evaluator were preempted. It retained scores for 43/50 tasks: 41 rubric-graded submissions with both reports, one confirmed missing-submission zero, and one setup-failure zero. Seven tasks remain unresolved. The mean over the 43 scored tasks is **74.56/100**; it is not a complete 50-task score. Allowing each unresolved grade to range from 0 to 100 gives an all-50 range of 64.12–78.12. Both Iris jobs are terminal and a full Daytona inventory found zero owned sandboxes remaining.

The baseline is the [Snowball v0.1 run and trace audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6297505720). Both runs use the same 50 public tasks, inputs, Harbor/Pi revisions, context and output budgets, time limits, retry policy, MiniMax judge, and signed rubric scorer. GLM uses its supported serving interface; Snowball used its own serving and tool parser. The GLM service did not report an exact weights revision, and sampling/serving defaults were not independently matched. This is a comparison of the two model-serving systems under a shared evaluation setup.

| First attempt, all 50 tasks | Snowball v0.1 | GLM-5.3 |
|---|---:|---:|
| At least one nonempty report retained | 12 | 35 |
| Both `trace.md` and `answer.txt` retained | 5 | 35 |
| Confirmed missing submission | 36 | 1 |
| Submission unverified after verifier failure | 2 | 14 |
| Native rewards available | 48 | 34 |
| Sum of available scores, in points | 212 | 2,623 |
| All-50 mean allowing each unavailable score to range from 0 to 100 | 4.24–8.24 | 52.46–84.46 |

These ranges bound the effect of unavailable grades; they are not confidence intervals. Even assigning every unavailable GLM grade zero and every unavailable Snowball grade 100 leaves a large gap. GLM retained reports on 23 of the 36 tasks where Snowball's first attempt had a confirmed missing submission.

“Unverified” means the verifier did not retain the reports and did not produce a missing-submission verdict. It does not establish whether files existed in the sandbox. The GLM first attempts include two judge failures with both reports retained, in addition to the 14 cases with unverified submissions.

The traces reveal three distinct problems:

- GLM's confirmed missing submission, `da-3-5`, performed 27 tool calls before an empty assistant response with normal `stop` and one output token. No executed tool arguments mentioned either required report filename. This was not an observed context/output-limit stop. spillover_issues.author: karansag
spillover_issues.body:
Resuming from a committed epoch checkpoint into a root containing later uncommitted checkpoints can fail on the next save. A 32-H100 Snowball SFT continuation restored step 320, completed the remaining 642 updates, then failed while finalizing an asynchronous save into the existing step-641 directory:

```text
ValueError: FAILED_PRECONDITION: Error opening "zarr3" driver:
Expected "chunk_shape" of [2560] but received: [80]
array: model/transformer/blocks/1/rms_attn/weight
checkpoint: checkpoints/step-641/
```

The checkpoint barrier subsequently timed out after 30 minutes, and the gang exited before producing its final HF export.

Reproduce:
1. Train with permanent epoch checkpoints at zero-based steps 320, 641 and 962. Interrupt the run while later checkpoint writes are incomplete, leaving `step-320/metadata.json` committed, a step-641 TensorStore payload without `metadata.json`, and a manifest-only step-962 directory.
2. Resume from the committed step-320 checkpoint with the same output root. Keep the incomplete later directories in place.
3. Continue through the remaining epoch boundaries. In the observed continuation, the save requested chunk shape `[2560]` for an array whose partial write stored `[80]`. TensorStore raised the error above; the asynchronous failure surfaced at the terminal checkpoint hook, after training had completed. The reason the requested chunk shape changed after restore has not yet been isolated, so this is an observed reproduction rather than a reduced deterministic test.

Observed on `cw-rno2a`, 2026-10-21, with four eight-H100 tasks, batch 16 × 32,768, eight-way expert parallelism, four-way context parallelism, and native checkpoints every 321 updates. Both the original run and continuation used `11d41241ec`, `experiments/post_training/agentic_sweep/arms.py`, and `--parent v0.1 --arm relay --data-variant low --learning-rate 1e-6 --epochs 3 --hf-export-schedule final-only`. No mesh or optimizer change was requested on resume. The original coordinator `/karan/arm-train-relay-low-v0p1-v7-20261021-cw-rno2a` was killed at 18:47 UTC during the controller outage in #10433. Its root retained a committed step 320 (16:48 UTC), an uncommitted step-641 payload (17:49–17:54 UTC), and a manifest-only step 962 (18:30 UTC).

Continuation `/karan/arm-train-relay-low-v0p1-v7-20261021-cw-rno2a-r3`, at `11d41241ec`, selected step 320 at 19:20 UTC. It reached step 641 at 20:09 UTC and the last optimizer update, step 962, at 20:41 UTC. At 21:11 UTC the terminal hook surfaced the step-641 chunk-layout error and checkpoint barrier timeout. Fresh object reads found neither a step-641 nor a step-962 commit marker. The original partial directories are preserved under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/checkpoints/karan/relay-low-v0.1-v7-20261021-lr1e-06-3ep/2026.10.21/checkpoints/`.

Two plain SFT runs using the same batch size and mesh committed their epoch saves in clean roots; those runs exported HF after epoch 2 and at the final step. A third plain SFT run using final-only HF exports also committed its first epoch, step 205, in a clean root. These observations show that final-only HF exports alone do not prevent native saves; they do not isolate every condition needed for the chunk-layout mismatch.

Expected: On resume, identify later step directories lacking a commit marker and remove or version those incomplete writes before reusing their step numbers. A terminal checkpoint write should start in an empty directory when a stale incomplete directory exists, without reopening its incompatible arrays. Preserve committed checkpoints, and report asynchronous save failures before allowing an entire additional epoch to run.

Related: #9380 reports a chunk-layout mismatch when rewriting an already committed final checkpoint after a resume with no new optimizer updates. This case concerns uncommitted later checkpoints encountered while continuing from an earlier committed epoch. Part of #10213.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

Checkpoint discovery requires `metadata.json`, so the continuation correctly restored step 320 while leaving the uncommitted step 641 payload in place. `Checkpointer` then reused the fixed `step-641` destination; TensorStore opened arrays already carrying a different chunk grid. The previous asynchronous save is checked at the next save or during trainer exit, which can delay the error until another epoch has run.

**Relevant code**
- [`checkpoint.py#L638-L667`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e524e9e12773de7be3f1e7fd8fc80c8d356ef275/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py#L638-L667) — fixed step destination
- [`checkpoint.py#L840-L915`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e524e9e12773de7be3f1e7fd8fc80c8d356ef275/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py#L840-L915) — completion marker follows writes
- [`checkpoint.py#L1217-L1243`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e524e9e12773de7be3f1e7fd8fc80c8d356ef275/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py#L1217-L1243) — committed-directory discovery
- [`tensorstore_serialization.py#L678-L820`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e524e9e12773de7be3f1e7fd8fc80c8d356ef275/lib/levanter/src/levanter/tensorstore_serialization.py#L678-L820) — prior-save wait and array open
- [`trainer.py#L412-L430`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e524e9e12773de7be3f1e7fd8fc80c8d356ef275/lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py#L412-L430) — final asynchronous wait

# Proposed Fix

Give each save invocation a fresh checkpoint directory, such as `step-641-<save-id>`, with one ID chosen on process 0 and shared across the gang. Keep `metadata.json` as the completion marker and numeric step as its source of truth. Existing `step-N` checkpoints remain readable; a resumed save never reopens a prior attempt's arrays, including an uncommitted attempt or a committed final-step save (#9380). This avoids deleting an old writer's payload while it may still be active.

Audit readers and operational scripts that assume an exact `step-N` directory name. Discovery already reads the step from metadata, but direct path construction may need updating. Add a nonblocking check of completed asynchronous saves to each training checkpoint hook and before final hooks/export. Raise the original failure as soon as the background commit finishes while preserving asynchronous training when it is still running.

Test with local TensorStore data: leave a step 641 payload with incompatible chunk metadata and no commit marker, restore step 320, save step 641, and verify that the new checkpoint loads while the old payload and committed step 320 are untouched. Cover a repeated committed final step, cross-process agreement on the save path, and a real failed asynchronous write reported before the next scheduled save. Keep orphan cleanup separate from the save path; it needs an age threshold and an inactive-writer check before deleting object-store data.

The path change reaches checkpoint producers, direct-path consumers, and asynchronous trainer error handling, so this needs a design and regression pass rather than a one-line overwrite fix. No open PR matched #10453 or the chunk-layout failure. The remaining decision is the retention window for abandoned attempt directories; it does not block save isolation.

So the epoch-2 save path itself works; the failure above is specific to resuming into a root that already holds uncommitted partial step directories.

```

It requests 963 total updates and restores 321 completed updates, leaving 642. No mesh change was requested. The old root's later partial directories remain evidence, not valid restore points.

spillover_issues.author: davidlundgren
spillover_issues.body:
Snowball/Grug checkpoints back to the 09.21 Datakit SFT model sometimes write more than one thinking segment in a single assistant message. The usual form is a think block followed by a second segment closed by a stray `<|end_think|>` with no matching `<|start_think|>`. Smartie RL step 14 also stacks complete near-duplicate blocks with nothing between them:

```
<|start_think|>We need to see the files first. Let's list them and examine content.<|end_think|><|start_think|>We need to inspect the files to understand the corrections. Let's list and view them.<|end_think|><|start_think|>We need to see the content. Let's run ls to see files.<|end_think|><|start_think|>I'll list the files in the workspace.<|end_think|>
```

The `grug` reasoning parser moves only the first segment into `reasoning`. It splits at the first `<|start_think|>` and the first `<|end_think|>` ([`basic_parsers.py:157`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/3a054c458ca8a32609ba2bc578c4d9b93eabb395/vllm/reasoning/basic_parsers.py#L157), inherited by [`grug_reasoning_parser.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/3a054c458ca8a32609ba2bc578c4d9b93eabb395/vllm/reasoning/grug_reasoning_parser.py)). Later segments stay in `content` with raw think tags, so users and LLM judges see them. Tool calls after the segments still parse.

The same Smartie conversations also show long thinking-only loops that hit the token limit with an empty reply, for example `\n\nNow.` repeated 7,986 times.

Reproduce:
1. Open case `108de5fc` in the [Smartie step 14 vs Qwen 3.6 comparison](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/25f504c6-c6fb-4e14-8401-07dd8e6fbfba/v/28/?run=smartie-rl-step14-vs-qwen36-20261019-v3-final4#108de5fc029a4b65adb39205bdae818e).
2. Round 0, first assistant message: the reply text contains four stacked think blocks before the `ls` tool call.
3. Rounds 2 and 3: the turns end at `finish_reason=length` with no reply.

Expected: at most one think block per assistant message, as rendered by `MARIN_CHAT_TEMPLATE` (`lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_template.py:108`).

Rate by checkpoint on bixbench-pi (eval campaign `eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled`, first 20 tasks per run, final attempt). An assistant message counts when it has two or more thinking segments: a `<|end_think|>` in the text plus a parsed reasoning field, or two or more `<|end_think|>` in raw text.

| Checkpoint | Eval run | Tasks affected | Thinking messages affected |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21 | `20261017-022041-…-bixbench-pi-9e72…` | 6/20 | 19/762 (2.5%) |
| …-2026.09.21-dr-doom | `20261004-053226-…-bixbench-pi-4208` | 8/20 | 16/215 (7.4%) |
| Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02 | `20261003-114254-…-bixbench-pi-ec3e` | 8/20 | 17/279 (6.1%) |
| Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign2-DARE-TIES-02-2026.10.10 | `20261011-111055-…-bixbench-pi-cd7f` | 2/20 | 4/207 (1.9%) |
| Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14 | `20261019-104831-…-bixbench-pi-72d5` | 10/20 | 24/263 (9.1%) |

Run paths are under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/`; trajectories are `results/harbor_jobs/*/<task>/attempts/*/agent/pi.txt`. In the SFT and Dr. Doom runs, every affected message has exactly two segments. Smartie messages reach five segments.

ShellSim comparison applet, 150 random completed agentic cases per run, counting messages whose parsed `content` or `reasoning` still contains a think tag:

| Checkpoint | Parser | Cases with leftover tags | Messages with leftover tags |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| …-2026.09.21-dr-doom | grug_optional | 0/150 | 0/4,859 |
| Antidoom RLVR1 step 12 | grug_optional | 32/150 | 40/2,148 |
| Antidoom RLVR1 step 12 | grug | 47/150 | 94/2,688 |
| Merge-NUPA-BFCL-Shared100-2026.10.09 | grug | 146/150 | 294/1,757 |
| Merge-Campaign3-DARE-Linear-02-2026.10.12 | grug | 42/150 | 63/2,699 |
| Smartie RL step 14 | grug | 127/150 | 410/2,666 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (reference) | qwen3 | 0/150 | 0/2,742 |

`grug_optional` appears to drop stray `<|end_think|>` tags. That hides the two-segment form, so the Dr. Doom zero in the applet does not mean Dr. Doom is clean.

Open questions:
- Source in training data. A sample of 7 rendered SFT sources on `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rendered/sft/` (nemotron-terminal, agenttrove, openthoughts-agent-sft-100k, gpt-oss-rollouts, glm-5.2-kernelgym-rollouts, coderforge, massive_function_calling; 178k assistant turns) has no turn with more than one think block. These sources are about 10% of the 09.21 SFT tokens. `nemotron_sft_v3` (55%), `open_swe_traces`, and `penfever-traces` were not checked.
- Why the rate rises through RL and merging. Smartie has the highest message rate and the longest stacks; its initializer has the lowest rate in this sample. 20 tasks per checkpoint is a small sample.

Related: #10305 (Smartie RLVR), #9691 (Dr. Doom de-looping).

comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The reported raw generations contain consecutive think blocks; the Smartie step-14 sample has leftover tags in 127/150 cases, versus 0/150 for the Dr. Doom SFT control. The Marin template renders at most one think block per assistant message, while the pinned vLLM parser extracts only the first block, exposing later blocks in `content`. The exact-periodic-suffix loop detector cannot establish whether paraphrased blocks were penalized; the first bad training stage and the proposed FTPO cause remain unverified.

**Relevant code**
- [`chat_template.py#L105-L114`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/036702ca09e1498893582ce1ec6e8e2f04c1bcff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_template.py#L105-L114) — renders one reasoning span.

- [`trajectory_reward_shaping.py#L262-L294`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/036702ca09e1498893582ce1ec6e8e2f04c1bcff/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/trajectory_runners/trajectory_reward_shaping.py#L262-L294) — detects exact periodic tails.
